ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r4.claim: The David and Solomon miracles answer the preceding denials of resurrection: unbelievers could not reject extraordinary events already attested by their reports and poetry, including singing mountains, softened iron, subjected wind, flowing copper, and jinn labor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r4.anchor: هي أن أولئك الكفار أنكروا البعث لاستحالته عندهم، فأخبروا بوقوع ما هو مستحيل في العادة مما لا يمكنهم إنكاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r5.claim: An alternative link is that, after mentioning those who turn back to God, the passage gives David as an example of repentance and God's gifts to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r5.anchor: وقيل: لما ذكر من ينيب من عباده، ذكر من جملتهم داود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r6.claim: Another explanation says the gifts to David and Solomon show that God's gifts to Muhammad are not impossible; after the parallel, the narrative returns to Sabaʾ and its destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r6.anchor: وقيل: ذكر نعمته على داود وسليمان، عليهما السلام، احتجاجا على ما منح محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r7.claim: Reported gifts to David include the Psalms, just judgment, reliance on God, and the subjection of mountains and birds and softening of iron.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r7.anchor: والفضل الذي أوتي داود: الزبور، والعدل في القضاء، والثقة بالله، وتسخير الجبال، والطير، وتليين الحديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r8.claim: Ya Jibāl may be introduced by an implied saying, either as a verbal noun apposed to faḍlan or as a verb apposed to ātaynā, or as an independent “We said.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r8.anchor: يا جبال: هو إضمار القول، إما مصدر، أي قولنا يا جبال، فيكون بدلا من فضلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r9.claim: Addressing mountains as obedient rational listeners signals that all creatures and inanimate things submit to God's will, displaying divine sovereignty and majesty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r9.anchor: وجعل الجبال بمنزلة العقلاء الذين إذا أمرهم أطاعوا وأذعنوا، وإذا دعاهم سمعوا وأجابوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r10.claim: Most readers recite awibi as a doubled form of āba, meaning “glorify with him,” as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أوبي، مضاعف آب يؤب، ومعناه: سبحي معه، قاله ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r11.speaker: مؤرج، وأبو ميسرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r11.claim: Muʾarrij and Abu Maysara say awibi means “glorify” in the language of Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p523/r11.anchor: وقال مؤرج، وأبو ميسرة: أوبي: سبحي، بلغة الحبشة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r1.claim: The doubled awibi is causative rather than intensive: āba is intransitive “return,” made transitive as “return the glorification with him.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r1.anchor: رجع اللازم فعدي بالتضعيف، إذ شرحوه بقولهم: رجعي معه التسبيح.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r2.claim: Zamakhshari says God created glorification within the mountains as He created speech in the tree, so they audibly glorified as a miracle for David.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ومعنى تسبيح الجبال: أن الله يخلق فيها تسبيحا، كما خلق الكلام في الشجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says Zamakhshari's comparison reflects the Muʿtazilite view that Moses heard speech created in the tree, not God's speech itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r3.anchor: يعني أن الذي يسمع موسى هو مما خلقه الله في الشجرة من الكلام، لا أنه كلام الله حقيقة، وهو مذهب المعتزلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r4.claim: One report says David lamented his sin in a sorrowful, repeated tune, with mountains echoing and birds joining his song.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r4.anchor: قيل: كان ينوح على ذنبه بترجيع وتحزين، وكانت الجبال تساعده على نوحه بأصدائها والطير بأصواتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the echo explanation: an echo is not truly a mountain's voice or action, and God commanded mountains themselves to glorify; only the claim that God made them speak fits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r5.anchor: فليس بشيء، لأن الصدى ليس بصوت الجبال حقيقة، والله تعالى نادى الجبال وأمرها بأن تؤوب معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reads awibi as “travel with him”; taʾwīb is daytime travel after a night journey, as the cited line uses awbū al-sayr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: معنى أوبي معه: سيري معه أين سار، والتأويب: سير النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r7.speaker: تميم بن مقبل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r7.claim: Tamim ibn Muqbil's phrase awbū al-sayr supports the sense of resuming travel by day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r7.anchor: لحقنا بحي أوبوا السير بعد ما ... رفعنا شعاع الشمس والطرف تجنح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r8.claim: A second poetic line uses taʾwīb for a day of travel toward enemies, supporting the daytime-travel gloss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r9.claim: Another gloss takes awibi as “act with him as he acts”; when David recited the Psalms, mountains sounded with him and birds listened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r9.anchor: وقيل: أوبي: تصرفي معه على ما يتصرف فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة، وابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r10.claim: These readers recite awibi as an imperative from awb, “return with him,” whether in glorification or travel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة، وابن أبي إسحاق: أوبي، أمر من أوب: أي رجعي معه في التسبيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r11.claim: A feminine singular command can address a nonrational plural such as mountains; the source cites يا خيل الله اركبي and another line, noting the latter agreement with rational feminine nouns is rare.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r11.anchor: فأمر الجبال كأمر الواحدة المؤنثة، لأن جمع ما لا يعقل يجوز فيه ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r12.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r12.claim: Sibawayh reports Abu ʿAmr's parsing of accusative al-ṭayr as coordinated with the syntactic position of the vocative mountains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r12.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: والطير، بالنصب عطفا على موضع يا جبال. قال سيبويه: وقال أبو عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r13.claim: Abu ʿAmr supplies an implied verb, “and We subjected the birds to him,” for the accusative reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r13.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: بإضمار فعل تقديره: وسخرنا له الطير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r14.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r14.claim: Al-Kisaʾi coordinates accusative al-ṭayr with faḍlan, meaning that the birds' glorification was also a gift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r14.anchor: وقال الكسائي: عطفا على فضلا، أي وتسبيح الطير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r15.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses accusative al-ṭayr as a comitative object, but Abu Hayyan rejects this because maʿahu already precedes it and two such objects require coordination or substitution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r15.anchor: وقال الزجاج: نصبه على أنه مفعول معه. انتهى، وهذا لا يجوز، لأن قبله معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r16.speaker: السلمي، وابن هرمز، وأبو يحيى، وأبو نوفل، ويعقوب، وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r16.claim: These readers, along with a group of Medinans and a transmission from ʿAsim, raise al-ṭayr: it may coordinate with the vocal form of ya jibāl or the pronoun in awibi, or be a subject with omitted predicate “the birds return.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r16.anchor: وقرأ السلمي، وابن هرمز، وأبو يحيى، وأبو نوفل، ويعقوب، وابن أبي عبلة، وجماعة من أهل المدينة، وعاصم في رواية: والطير، بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r5.speaker: بعض الباطنية أو من يشبههم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r5.claim: Some esoteric interpreters reduce mountain glorification to the general statement that everything praises God, and the wind to Solomon's training swift horses; they absurdly reduce a month's morning journey to one farsakh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r5.anchor: لبعض الباطنية، أو من يشبههم، تحريف في هذه الجمل. إن تسبيح الجبال هو نوع قوله: وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r4.claim: David's armor suits his need to fight enemies, while Solomon's buildings, statues, and vessels suit his peaceful kingship, secured by his father so no one could challenge him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r4.anchor: وذكر في حق داود اشتغاله بآلة الحرب لاحتياجه إلى قتال الأعداء، وفي حق سليمان المحاريب والتماثيل

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.claim: After its critique of disbelievers, the sūrah briefly recalls the accomplishments of David and Solomon.
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.anchor: Brief allusions to the accomplishments of the prophets David (vv. 10–11) and Solomon (vv. 12–14)

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r3.claim: The command means that God told the mountains to repeat praise with David as often as he repeated it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r3.anchor: المعنى فقلنا يا جبال أوبي معه،

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r4.claim: Another reading means “return with him”; the root آب يؤوب means to return, here returning praise with David.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ (أوبي معه) فمعناه رجعي معه، يقال آب يؤوب

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r5.claim: On the nominative reading, الطير may coordinate with the understood subject of أوبي: mountains and birds together repeat praise.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r5.anchor: أن يكون نسقا على ما في (أوبي)، المعنى يا جبال رجعي

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r6.claim: Alternatively, nominative الطير is an apposition: the call addresses both the mountains and the birds.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مرفوعا عل البدل. المعنى: يا جبال

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that accusative الطير coordinates with آتينا: God bestowed the birds on David and subjected them to him.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r7.anchor: حكى ذلك أبو عبيدة عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء،

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r8.claim: Accusative الطير can be a vocative coordinated with the underlying accusative position of جبال; Basran grammarians place every vocative in the accusative syntactic position.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نصبا على النداء. المعنى: يا جبال أوبي معه

ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r9.claim: Accusative الطير can instead express accompaniment, as in قمت وزيدا: the mountains and birds praise with David.
ZAJJAJ:v4p242/r9.anchor: كما تقول: قمت وزيدا، أي قمت مع زيد

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r1.claim: God made iron soft for David; it yielded like threads so he could make armor.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r1.anchor: جعلناه لينا كالخيوط يطاوعه حتى عمل الدروع.

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r2.claim: David was the first to make coats of mail; before him, iron protection consisted of pieces like cuirasses.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r2.anchor: وأول من عمل الدروع داود، وكان ما يستجن به من الحديد

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n10/r1.claim: Asad connects David's special favor with the preceding elliptical reference to repentance and cites 38:24, where David recognizes his sin and repents.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n10/r1.anchor: This connects with the elliptic reference to repentance in the preceding verse: David is singled out for special mention in view of the allusion

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n11/r1.claim: Asad links the mountains and birds praising with David to the parallel passage at 21:79.

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r1.claim: Hadid primarily means sharp, concretely or abstractly; Asad cites 50:22 and Arabic idioms for sharp intellect, bold sight, and a sharp odor.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r1.anchor: The term hadid denotes, primarily, something that is "sharp" in both the concrete and abstract senses of the word

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r2.claim: The definite form al-hadid may denote sharpness or iron; the latter allows a literal soft-iron rendering.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r2.anchor: An alternative rendering of the above phrase would be: "We caused iron to become soft for him"

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r3.claim: Asad reads the softening of sharpness as an allusion to David's aesthetic sensibility in the Psalms, goodness, and humility.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r3.anchor: God's having "softened all sharpness" in David is evidently an allusion to his exalted sense of beauty (expressed in the poetry of his Psalms) as well as to his goodness and humility.

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r4.claim: As an alternative, Asad allows a literal softening of iron, alluding to David's gifts as poet, warrior, and ruler.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n12/r4.anchor: An alternative rendering of the above phrase would be: "We caused iron to become soft for him", which might be an allusion to his outstanding abilities as poet, warrior and ruler.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r1.claim: Poetic lines use awba for returning: every absent person returns, unlike the dead, and the traveler is welcomed back.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r1.anchor: وكل ذى غيبة يئوب. . . وغائب الموت لا يئوب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r2.claim: The Qur'an has iyāb once, maʾāb nine times, awʾiba in this verse, and awāb five times singular plus once plural.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p470/r2.anchor: ومعها من المادة (مآب) تسع مرات، و (أوَّبى) في آية سبأ 10، و (أوَّاب) مفردا خمس مرات

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the mountains’ response with David as glorifying God with him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ يا جبال أوبي معه ﴾ قال سبحي معه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r1.claim: Qatada says God softened iron for David so he could work it without fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وألنا له الحديد ﴾ قال لينه الله له يعمله بغير نار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r1.claim: Alusi prefers understanding God's favor as gracious beneficence bestowed on David for his excellent turning back to God and sound repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r1.anchor: أي آتيناه لحسن إنابته وصحة توبته فضلا أي نعمة وإحسانا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r2.claim: One view takes the favor as an extra distinction over prophets who preceded David, or over the prophets of Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r2.anchor: وقيل فضلا وزيادة على سائر الأنبياء المتقدمين عليه أو أنبياء بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r3.claim: Another view says David was favored above everyone except Muhammad, since every prophetic virtue was also given to Muhammad actually or potentially, though he did not display some of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r3.anchor: أو على ما عدا نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه ماا من فضيلة في أحد من الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r4.claim: A further view makes David superior to all prophets, while allowing that a lesser-ranked prophet may have a unique gift; David is singled out here for the favor named in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r4.anchor: أو على الأنبياء مطلقا وقد يكون في المفضول ما ليس في غيره وقد انفرد عليه السلام بما ذكر ههنا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r5.claim: Another interpretation extends David's superiority over all people, including through prophecy, scripture, kingship, and a beautiful voice; Alusi objects that neither kingship nor voice is unique separately, while the combination is not unique among prophets.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r5.anchor: وقيل : أو على سائر الناس فيندرج فيه النبوة والكتاب والملك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r6.claim: Alusi takes faḍl as beneficence, made indefinite for magnification; from Us emphasizes its inherent and relational grandeur, and is placed before the object for focus and anticipation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r6.anchor: وأنا أرى الفضل لتفسير الفضل بالإحسان وتنكيره للتفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r7.claim: The mention of David and Solomon here fits the preceding description of a sign for every servant who turns back to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r7.anchor: وذكر شؤن داؤد وسليمان عليهما السلام هنا لمناسبة ذكر المنيب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the stories to disbelievers denying resurrection: the account confronts them with extraordinary events that their own reports and poetry make hard to deny.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : مناسبة قصتيهما عليهما السلام لما قبلها هي أن أولئك الكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r9.claim: Another explanation sees David and Solomon's gifts as evidence that God's favors to Muhammad should not be considered surprising; after this example, the discourse returns to the destruction of Sabaʾ for disbelief and defiance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r9.anchor: وقيل : ذكر سبحانه نعمته عليهما احتجاجا على ما منح نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd explain the command to the mountains as glorify with David, echoing his praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r10.anchor: أي سبحي معه قاله إبن عباس وقتادة وإبن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r11.speaker: أبو ميسرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r11.claim: Ibn Jarīr transmits from Abū Maysara that the word means this in the language of Abyssinia.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r11.anchor: وأخرجه إبن جرير عن أبي ميسرة إلا أنه قال : معناه ذلك بلغة الحبشة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r12.claim: Alusi says the apparent sense is Arabic, from taʾwīb: return and repeat the glorification with David.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r12.anchor: والظاهر أنه عربي من التأويب والمراد رجعي معه التسبيح وردديه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the original past form is āba, doubled for intensification; Abū Ḥayyān counters that doubling makes the originally intransitive verb transitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p112/r13.anchor: وقال إبن عطية : إن أصل ماضيه آب وضعف للمبالغة وتعقبه في البحر بقوله ويظهر أن التضعيف للتعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r1.claim: When David glorified God, the mountains glorified in a voice audible from them; God can make them glorify audibly, as pebbles glorified in the Prophet's hand and were also heard in Abū Bakr's hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r1.anchor: يروى أنه عليه السلام كان إذا سبح سبحت الجبال مثل تسبيحه بصوت يسمع منها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r2.claim: Some say God first created understanding in the mountains, then addressed and commanded them as beings capable of understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r2.anchor: ولا يبعد على هذا أن يقال : إنه تعالى خلق فيها الفهم أولا فناداها كما ينادي أولوا الفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r3.claim: Another explanation treats the mountains as rational beings to show that every animal and inanimate thing submits to God's will, displaying divine sovereignty and majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه سبحانه نزل الجبال منزلة العقلاء الذين إذا أمرهم أطاعوا وأذعنوا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r4.claim: Some interpret the command as mountains prompting David to glorify through reflection on them; Alusi rejects it as contrary to transmitted interpretation, contradicted by with him, and not a distinctive merit or miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد بتأويلها حملها إياه على التسبيح إذا تأمل ما فيها وفيه مع كونه خلاف المأثور

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r5.claim: Another view says David lamented his sin in a repeated sorrowful chant and the mountains joined through their echoes; Alusi objects that an echo is not truly the mountain's voice and that everyone gets echoes.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r5.anchor: وقيل : كان عليه السلام ينوح على ذنبه بترجيع وتحزين وكانت الجبال تسعده بأصدائها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes taʾwīb as traveling by day with David, as one who travels at night resumes or repeats the journey during daylight.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r6.anchor: وعن الحسن أن معنى ( أوبي معه ) سيري معه أين سار والتأويب سير النهار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r7.speaker: تميم بن مقبل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r7.claim: Tamīm ibn Muqbil's line uses awbū al-sayr for resuming or continuing a journey after the sun's rays have departed.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك قول تميم بن مقبل : لحقنا بحي أوبوا السير بعدما دفعنا شعاع الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r8.speaker: قول آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r8.claim: An anonymous second verse contrasts days of settled gatherings with a day of journeying to enemies, using taʾwīb for travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r8.anchor: وقول آخر : يومان يوم مقامات وأندية ويوم سير إلى الأعداء تأويب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r9.claim: Alusi rejects the travel interpretation because mountains are the earth's pegs and there is no report that they traveled with David or anyone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r9.anchor: وأورد عليه أن الجبال أوتاد الأرض ولم ينقل سيرها مع داؤد عليه السلام أو غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r10.claim: Some say the mountains accompanied David in whatever he did, praising, lamenting, or reciting the Psalms; Alusi says taʾwīb is not known in Arabic to mean such varied action.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r10.anchor: وقيل : المعنى تصرفي معه على ما يتصرف فيه فكانت إذا سبح سبحت وإذا ناح ناحت

ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r11.claim: A further interpretation has the mountains return to David's intent in digging, finding springs, extracting minerals, or laying roads; the command is construed as an appositional or independent clause, though Abū Ḥayyān dislikes the independent reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p113/r11.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أرجعي إلى مراده فيما يريد من حفر واستنباط أعين واستخراج معدن ووضع طريق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة وابن أبي إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r1.claim: These authorities read awībī with ḍamma on the hamza and a still wāw, as an imperative of awb, to return.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r1.anchor: وقرأ إبن عباس والحسن وقتادة وإبن أبي إسحاق ( أوبي ) بضم الهمزة وسكون الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes awb, used only of animals with will, from rujuʿ, which applies to both animals and inanimate things.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r2.anchor: وفرق بينهما الراغب بأن الأوب لا يقال إلا في الحيوان الذي له إرادة والرجوع يقال فيه وفي غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r3.claim: On this reading, the majority understand the mountains as returning with David in glorification; a feminine singular command is permitted with a nonrational plural, as in calls to horses and other examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r3.anchor: والمعنى على هذه القراءة عند الجمهور أرجعي معه في التسبيح وأمر الجبال كأمر الواحدة المؤنثة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r4.claim: The same feminine singular agreement can occasionally occur with a feminine rational plural, illustrated by a poet's command to women to remain.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r4.anchor: وقد جاء ذلك في جمع من يعقل من المؤنث قال الشاعر : تركنا الخيل والنعم المفدى وقلنا للنساء بها أقيمي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr construes the accusative al-ṭayr with an omitted verb: and We subjected the birds to David.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r5.anchor: بالنصب وهو عند أبي عمرو بن العلاء بإضمار فعل تقديره وسخرنا له الطير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports Abū ʿAmr also allowed coordination with faḍlan, since giving David the birds amounts to subjecting them to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r6.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيدة عنه إن ذاك بالعطف على ( فضلا ) ولا حاجة إلى الإضمار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī cites the poetic example I fed her straw and cold water as a parallel construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r7.anchor: وذكر الطيبي أن ذلك كقوله : علفتها تبنا وماء باردا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r8.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī also coordinates the birds, supplying the omitted noun their glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي : بالعطف أيضا إلا أنه قدر مضافا أي وتسبيح الطير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r9.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r9.claim: Sībawayh coordinates al-ṭayr with the syntactic position of the vocative mountains, citing a poetic parallel; some grammarians object because a definite noun with al cannot be directly vocative, while its proponents allow dependent forms that cannot stand alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r9.anchor: وقال سيبويه : الطير معطوف على محل ( جبال )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats the accusative as a comitative object; Abū Ḥayyān objects that maʿahu already supplies accompaniment and two such objects require coordination or apposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو منصوب على أنه مفعول معه وتعقبه أبو حيان بأنه لا يجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r11.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r11.claim: Al-Khafājī replies that maʿahu may be an adverb or circumstantial expression, not a comitative object, so Abū Ḥayyān's objection does not hold.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r11.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : لا يأباه ( معه ) سواء تعلق بأوبي على أنه ظرف لغو أو جعل حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r12.claim: Alusi calls it an especially bad defense to claim the conjunction was omitted to avoid adjacent wāws or that the second relation was delayed until after the first.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114/r12.anchor: وأقبح من الذنب الاعتذار حيث أجيب بأنه يجوز أن يقال حذفت واو العطف من قوله تعالى : ( والطير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r1.speaker: السلمي وابن هرمز وأبو يحيى وأبو نوفل ويعقوب وابن أبي عبلة وجماعة من أهل المدينة وعاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r1.claim: Al-Sulamī, Ibn Hurmuz, Abū Yaḥyā, Abū Nawfal, Yaʿqūb, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, a group of Medinese, and ʿĀṣim in one narration read al-ṭayru in the nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وإبن هرمز وأبو يحيى وأبو نوفل ويعقوب وإبن أبي عبلة وجماعة من أهل المدينة وعاصم في رواية ( والطير ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r2.claim: The nominative reading can coordinate the birds with the surface form of mountains, whose vowel is incidental but resembles inflection; a dependent may use a form unavailable to the independent.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r2.anchor: وخرج على أنه معطوف على ( جبال ) باعتبار لفظه وحركته لعروضها تشبه حركة الإعراب ويغتفر في التابع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r3.claim: It may instead coordinate with the implicit subject of awībī, licensed by separation through the adverb.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معطوف على الضمير المستتر في ( أوبي ) وسوغ ذلك الفصل بالظرف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r4.claim: Another analysis supplies wa-li-taʾūba al-ṭayru, and another makes the birds a subject with an omitted predicate meaning they return.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو بتقدير ولتؤوب الطير نظير ما قيل في قوله تعالى : ( أسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r5.speaker: السدي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī and others say God made iron in David's hand like wax or dough, so he could shape it as he wished without fire or hammering.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r5.anchor: وألنا له الحديد ( وجعلناه في يده كالشمع والعجين يصرفه كما يشاء من غير نار ولا ضرب مطرقة قاله السدي وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r6.claim: Another view says iron was soft relative to the extraordinary strength given to David, just as wax is soft relative to the strength of ordinary people.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : جعلناه بالنسبة إلى قوته التي آتيناها إياه لينا كالشمع بالنسبة إلى قوى سائر البشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r11.claim: David’s special favor means prophethood and scripture; alternatives are kingship or all his gifts, including beautiful voice and softened iron.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r11.anchor: يعني النبوة والكتاب، وقيل: الملك. وقيل: جميع ما أوتي من حسن الصوت وتليين الحديد وغير ذلك مما خص به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r12.claim: God called the mountains to glorify along with David when he glorified.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r13.claim: Another explanation derives the form from returning: the mountains repeat their response with David.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r13.anchor: وقيل: هو تفعيل من الإياب وهو الرجوع، أي: رجعي معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r14.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r14.claim: Al-Qutaybi connects the word to taʾwib in travel, journeying all day and resting at night, hence glorifying with David throughout the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r14.anchor: وقال القتيبي: أصله من التأويب في السير، وهو أن يسير النهار كله وينزل ليلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r15.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r15.claim: Wahb explains the word as reciting with David.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p387/r15.anchor: كأنه قال أوبي النهار كله بالتسبيح معه. وقال وهب: نوحي معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r1.claim: Birds coordinate with mountains in the accusative, since vocatives are syntactically accusative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r1.anchor: عطف على موضع الجبال، لأن كل منادى في موضع النصب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r2.claim: Another explanation says God subjected the birds and commanded them to glorify with David.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه: وسخرنا وأمرنا الطير أن تسبح معه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r3.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads al-ṭayr in the nominative, coordinated with the mountains: respond, you and the birds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r3.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: "والطير" بالرفع ردا على الجبال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r4.claim: David's calls were answered by mountain echoes while birds circled above him; today's echoes come from this.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r4.anchor: وكان داود إذا نادى بالناحية أجابته الجبال بصداها وعكفت الطير عليه من فوقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r5.claim: One report says mountains answered David's glorification with glorification like his.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r5.anchor: وقيل: كان داود إذا تخلل الجبال فسبح الله جعلت الجبال تجاوبه بالتسبيح نحو ما يسبح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r6.claim: Another report says God made David hear the mountains' glorification when he tired, renewing his energy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r6.anchor: وقيل: كان داود عليه السلام إذا لحقه فتور أسمعه الله تسبيح الجبال تنشيطا له.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r7.claim: Iron became like wax or dough in David's hand and could be shaped without fire or a hammer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r7.anchor: كالشمع والعجين يعمل منه ما يشاء من غير نار ولا ضرب مطرقة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r8.speaker: الأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r8.claim: A reported story says David disguised himself to ask people about his rule; an angel criticized his use of the treasury to support his family, prompting him to seek independent provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r8.anchor: على ما روي في الأخبار: أن داود عليه السلام لما ملك بني إسرائيل كان من عادته أن يخرج للناس متنكرا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r9.speaker: الأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r9.claim: In that story God softened iron and taught David to make armor, making him the first to do so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r9.anchor: فألان الله تعالى له الحديد وعلمه صنعة الدرع، وإنه أول من اتخذها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r10.claim: One report says David sold each armor for four thousand dirhams, supporting his family and giving the rest to the poor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r10.anchor: ويقال: إنه كان يبيع كل درع بأربعة آلاف درهم، فيأكل ويطعم منها عياله ويتصدق منها على الفقراء والمساكين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r11.claim: Another says he made one armor daily for six thousand dirhams, spending two thousand on his family and giving four thousand to Israelite poor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r11.anchor: ويقال إنه كان يعمل كل يوم درعا يبيعها بستة آلاف درهم، فينفق ألفين منها على نفسه وعياله، ويتصدق بأربعة آلاف على فقراء بني إسرائيل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r12.claim: The Prophet said David ate only from the work of his own hand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388/r12.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كان داود عليه السلام لا يأكل إلا من عمل يده".

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r1.claim: David’s favor was either superiority over other prophets, as following gifts show, or all people, including prophethood, scripture, kingship, and beautiful voice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r1.anchor: أي على سائر الأنبياء وهو ما ذكر بعد، أو على سائر الناس

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r2.claim: The mountains return praise with David or lament over sin; God may create his voice in them, or contemplation may move them to praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r2.anchor: رجعي معه التسبيح أو النوحة على الذنب، وذلك إما بخلق صوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r3.claim: Another sense is that the mountains accompany David wherever he travels.

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r4.claim: A variant from awb means return to praise whenever David repeats it; parsed as apposition to “favor” or “We gave,” with an implied “We said.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r4.anchor: وقرىء «أوبي» من الأوب أي ارجعي في التسبيح

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r5.claim: Birds may coordinate with the mountains by syntax, with “favor,” or be an accusative accompaniment to “return”; nominative coordinates with the mountains’ expressed case.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r5.anchor: عطف على محل الجبال ويؤيده القراءة بالرفع عطفا على لفظها

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r6.claim: The nominative reading coordinates birds with the mountains’ expressed ending, treating the inherent ending as inflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r6.anchor: القراءة بالرفع عطفا على لفظها تشبيها للحركة البنائية العارضة بالحركة الإعرابية

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r7.claim: The wording portrays mountains and birds as rational beings obeying David, magnifying his stature and God’s dominion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r7.anchor: لما فيه من الفخامة والدلالة على عظم شأنه وكبرياء سلطانه، حيث جعل الجبال والطيور

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r8.claim: God made iron pliable in David’s hand like wax, shapeable without heating or hammering, through softening or strength.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:10/r8.anchor: جعلناه في يده كالشمع يصرفه كيف يشاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.claim: The wording clarifies that the favor comes from God alone, not through an intermediary as its source; the indefinite form magnifies the favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r1.anchor: بين أن الأمر ليس إلا منه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.claim: The favor also shows that no created thing can be brought into being independently of God’s will.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r2.anchor: وأنه لا يتوقف تكوين شيء على غير إرادته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.claim: Addressing mountains as rational beings who promptly obey dramatizes God’s complete power and control of all things.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r3.anchor: الجبال منزلة العقلاء الذين يبادرون إلى امتثال أوامره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.claim: The mountains echo David’s glorification, recitation of the Psalms, and other remembrance whenever he glorifies God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r4.anchor: رجعي التسبيح وقراءة الزبور وغيرهما من ذكر الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.claim: The mountains, the earth’s hardest substance, respond to a command as rational servants; this is an earthly sign of God’s power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r5.anchor: مما هو أشد الأرض بما هو وظيفة العقلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r6.claim: Birds, the lightest animals and vulnerable to falling if they die in flight, provide a heavenly sign of God’s power over the sky.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r6.anchor: عطف على ذلك أخف الحيوان وألطفه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r7.claim: The birds truly echoed David’s remembrance, like the birds’ own speech; their mention rules out the idea that the sound was merely an echo.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r7.anchor: فكانت ترجع معه الذكر فدل قرانها بالطير على ذكرها حقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r8.claim: Yaʿqūb reads al-ṭayr in the nominative, coordinating with the form of جبال; other readers coordinate with its syntactic position, while the conjunction may also mean with or imply an elided verb.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r8.anchor: أو تكون الواو بمعنى مع أو بتقدير فعل من معنى ما مضى كسخرنا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r9.speaker: وهب بن منبه
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r9.claim: Wahb b. Munabbih reports that David told the mountains to glorify and the birds to answer, then sang beautifully while reciting the Psalms.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r9.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : كان يقول للجبال : سبحي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r10.claim: Biqāʿī adduces reports that pebbles glorified in the hands of the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, and that food glorified while being eaten in the Prophet’s presence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r10.anchor: وكما كان الطعام يسبح في حضرته الشريفة وهو يؤكل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r11.claim: Biqāʿī also recalls reports that a stone greeted the Prophet, the house threshold and walls said amen to his prayer, and the trunk moaned.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r11.anchor: وأسكفة الباب وحوائط البيت تؤمن على دعائه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r12.claim: Biqāʿī adds reports that a lizard testified for the Prophet and that a camel complained when its eggs were taken, so the Prophet ordered them returned out of mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r12.anchor: وكما كان الضب يشهد له والجمل يشكو أخذ بيضها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r13.claim: God made iron, which originated in the mountains, as pliable in David’s hand as wax, so he could shape it without fire or hammer.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r13.anchor: الذي ولدناه من الجبال جعلناه في يده كالشمع يعمل منه ما يريد بلا نار ولا مطرقة

DURR-FULL:v6p674/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the command to the mountains as ‘glorify along with David.’
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {أوبي معه} قال: سبحي معه

DURR-FULL:v6p674/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r10.speaker: أبو ميسرة
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r10.claim: Abu Maysara says ‘glorify along with him’ is the meaning of the phrase in the Abyssinian language.
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r10.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة رضي الله عنه {أوبي معه} قال: سبحي معه بلسان الحبشة

DURR-FULL:v6p674/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses the command as glorification.
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {أوبي معه} قال: سبحي

DURR-FULL:v6p674/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r12.speaker: عكرمة وأبو عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r12.claim: Ikrima and Abu Abd al-Rahman give the same gloss: glorify with David.
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r12.anchor: عن عكرمة وأبي عبد الرحمن مثله

DURR-FULL:v6p674/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that the birds too glorify along with David.
DURR-FULL:v6p674/r13.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه في قوله {يا جبال أوبي معه والطير} أيضا يعني يسبح معه الطير

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r1.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r1.claim: Wahb says God commanded the mountains and birds to glorify with David whenever he glorified; the source repeats this report.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r1.anchor: عن وهب رضي الله عنه قال: أمر الله الجبال والطير أن تسبح مع داود عليه السلام إذا سبح

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd reads ‘the birds’ in the accusative and explains the construction as ‘We subjected the birds to him.’
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ (الطير) بالنصب بجملة قال: سخرنا له الطير

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the iron was softened for David like dough.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وألنا له الحديد} قال: كالعجين

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.claim: Qatada says David shaped softened iron by hand like clay into linked armor without fire or hammering; he was the first to make such armor, whereas earlier people used iron plates for protection.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وألنا له الحديد} قال: لين الله له الحديد فكان يسرده حلقا بيده يعمل به كما يعمل بالطين من غير أن يدخله النار ولا يضربه بمطرقة

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.claim: Hasan says the iron became dough-like in David’s hand so he could make armor from it.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {وألنا له الحديد} فيصير في يده مثل العجين فيصنع منه الدروع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that the birds, like the mountains, glorified God along with David.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r1.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا جبال اوبي معه والطير ايضا يعني يسبح معه الطير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd read al-ṭayr in the accusative, construing the phrase as “We subjected the birds to him.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه انه قرا ' الطير ' بالنصب بجملة قال : سخرنا له الطير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says iron became like dough in David’s hand, so he could make coats of mail from it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : والنا له الحديد يصير في يده مثل العجين ، فيصنع منه الدروع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r3.claim: The transition from the preceding passage to David is subtle and needs explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r3.anchor: مناسبة الانتقال من الكلام السابق إلى ذكر داود خفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says David and Solomon’s favor argues for the favor given to Muḥammad: God had bestowed such gifts on servants before.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عطية : ذكر الله نعمته على داود وسليمان احتجاجا على ما منح محمدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the returning servant reflects on God’s signs and recognizes His power over resurrection and punishment of deniers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r5.anchor: لأن المنيب لا يخلو من النظر في آيات الله على أنه قادر على كل شيء من البعث ومن عقاب من يكفر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r6.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r6.claim: Al-Ṭībī sees the mention of David as a smooth transition from the returning servant in 34:9, citing David’s description as one who repeatedly turns back to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r6.anchor: فقال الطيبي : فيه إشارة إلى بيان نظم هذه الآية بقوله : { ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا } لأنه كالتخلص منه إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r7.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī presents David as a model of repentance: from rough shepherd to chosen prophet and righteous king, his return to God brought worldly and afterlife favor and blessing to his descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r7.anchor: أن داود من أشهر المثل في المنيبين بما اشتهر به من انقلاب حاله بعد أن كان راعيا غليظا إلى أن اصطفاه الله نبيئا وملكا صالحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r8.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r8.claim: David’s favor teaches God’s care for those who return to Him and hints that Muḥammad’s rejection and hardship will likewise end in honor and a great community, as David’s did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r8.anchor: وفي ذكر فضله عبرة للناس بحسن عناية الله بالمنيبين تعريضا بضد ذلك للذين لم يعتبروا بآيات الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r9.claim: Although al-Ṭībī calls this transition takhalluṣ, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers istitrād or iʿtirāḍ; the return to polytheists shows their refutation remains the sūra’s main purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p154/r9.anchor: وسمى الطيبي هذا الانتقال إلى ذكر داود وسليمان تخلصا ، والوجه أن يسميه استطرادا أو اعتراضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r1.claim: Min in minnā marks origin and is governed by ātaynā: the favor came from God’s presence, honoring David’s gift.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r2.claim: The indefinite faḍlan magnifies David’s gifts: prophecy, kingship, community reform, just judgment, courage, abundance, self-sufficiency through armor craft, the Psalms, a beautiful voice, and a righteous long life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r2.anchor: وتنكير { فضلا } لتعظيمه وهو فضل النبوءة وفضل الملك ، وفضل العناية بإصلاح الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r3.claim: The mountains’ address is quoted speech with an omitted verb ‘He said’; deleting the speech verb is common, and this clause explains David’s favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r3.anchor: وجملة { يا جبال أوبي معه } مقول قول محذوف ، وحذف القول استعمال شائع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r4.claim: The compact wording conveys divine majesty, David’s stature, abundant meanings, and companionship through معه.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r4.anchor: وفي هذا الأسلوب الذي نظمت عليه الآية من الفخامة وجلالة الخالق وعظم شأن داود مع وفرة المعاني وإيجاز الألفاظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r5.claim: The command to the mountains is a creative command that subjugates them, not a request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r5.anchor: والأمر في { أوبي معه } أمر تكوين وتسخير .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r6.claim: Taʾwīb means echoing or repeating a sound; another reported view derives it from an Ethiopian word for glorification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r6.anchor: والتأويب : الترجيع ، أي ترجيع الصوت ، وقيل : التأويب بمعنى التسبيح لغة حبشية فهو من المعرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r7.speaker: يونس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r7.claim: The accusative ṭayr may coordinate with the vocative; a definite noun coordinated after a vocative can be nominative or accusative, with accusative preferred by Yūnus, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, and al-Jarmī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r7.anchor: والنصب أرجح عند يونس وأبي عمرو وعيسى بن عمر والجرمي وهو أوجه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r8.claim: Alternatively, ṭayr is a comitative object of awībī, meaning ‘echo with him and with the birds,’ so the birds join the praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { والطير } مفعولا معه ل { أوبي } . والتقدير : أوبي معه ومع الطير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r9.claim: God made iron pliable to David’s fingers so he could bend armor rings and press their rivets into place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r9.anchor: تسخيره لأصابعه حينما يلوي حلق الدروع ويغمز المسامير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.claim: An is explanatory: making iron pliable implied that God inspired David to use it by making full coats of mail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية لما في { ألنا له } من معنى : أشعرناه بتسخير الحديد ليقدم على صنعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r11.claim: The sūra had already introduced David as recipient of the Psalms in al-Nisāʾ and as a descendant of Abraham in al-Anʿām.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r11.anchor: وتقديم التعريف بداود عليه السلام عند قوله تعالى : { وآتينا داود زبورا في سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r1.claim: Iron is mineral earth that melts, softens, and can be hammered into shape when heated, then hardens as it cools.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r1.anchor: إذا صهر بالنار امتزج بعضه ببعض ولان وأمكن تطريقه وتشكيله فإذا برد تصلب

BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r1.claim: The name Dāwūd contains no connecting letters, suggesting that God wholly detached him from the world and honored him with hidden and manifest graces; names and titles descend from heaven.
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r1.anchor: أعطى الله تعالى داود اسما ليس فيه حروف الاتصال فدل على أنه قطعه عن العالم بالكلية وشرفه بألطافه الخفية والجلية

BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r2.claim: Faḍl means increase; its indefinite form signals a kind of favor that set David above the prophets, while superiority in one respect can coexist with inferiority in another.
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r2.anchor: والفضل الزيادة والتنوين للنوع أي : نوعا من الفضل على سائر الأنبياء مطلقا

BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r3.claim: The favor includes the mountains’ response, the birds’ subjection, and iron made pliable; these are special miracles, but do not exhaust David’s gifts, for God also gave him the Psalms.
BURSEVI:v7p207#2/r3.anchor: وهذا الفضل هو ما ذكر بعد من تأويب الجبال وتسخير الطير وإلانة الحديد فإنه معجزة خاصة به

BURSEVI:v7p208/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r1.claim: A questioner says that hearing the same remembrance as the spiritual traveler’s own would be an imaginary unveiling; a true unveiling hears a distinct remembrance from each thing.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r1.anchor: فمتى سمع السالك من الأشياء الذكر الذي هو مشغول به فكشفه خيالي غير صحيح يعني أنه خيال أقيم له في الموجودات

BURSEVI:v7p208/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r2.claim: The mountains’ agreement with David does not preclude their own distinct glorification, audible to him; alternatively, the wording means they traveled wherever he went, a miracle.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r2.anchor: لا يلزم من موافقة الجبال لداود أن لا يكون لها تسبيح آخر في نفسها مسموع لداود كما هي فيه والمعنى على الثاني سيرى معه حيث سار

BURSEVI:v7p208/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r3.claim: Al-ṭayr is accusative, coordinated with faḍlan: God subjected the birds to David, so no omitted verb or estimated phrase meaning their glorification is needed, unlike al-Irshād’s parsing.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r3.anchor: ولا إلى تقدير المضاف أي : تسبيح الطير

BURSEVI:v7p208/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r4.claim: The mountains and birds are addressed as rational beings; every animal and inanimate thing obeys God’s will and command.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r4.anchor: نزل الجبال والطير منزلة العقلاء حيث نوديت نداءهم إذ ما من حيوان وجماد إلا وهو منقاد لمشيئته ومطيع لأمره

BURSEVI:v7p208/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r5.claim: Since even immobile rocks and fleeing birds respond to David, hardened hearts are more blameworthy when they reject remembrance and flee or attack gatherings of truth.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r5.anchor: فانظر إذ من طبع الصخور الجمود ومن طبع الطيور النفور ومع هذا قد وافقته عليه السلام فأشد منها القاسية قلوبهم

BURSEVI:v7p208/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p208/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p208/r6.claim: Jāmī explains that David’s focused spirit transmitted glorification through his faculties and then to mountains and birds, reflections of those faculties; their praise’s reward therefore returned to him, not them.
BURSEVI:v7p208/r6.anchor: وإنما كان تسبيح الجبال والطير لتسبيحه لأنه لما قوي توجهه

BURSEVI:v7p209/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r1.claim: A Persian couplet suggests that every voice, spoken or silent, is a voice from the Beloved; hearing it makes the listener inwardly silent.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r1.anchor: همه آوازها در يش حق باز اكر يدا اكر وشيده آواز

BURSEVI:v7p209/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r2.claim: Līn means softness, first of bodies and by extension meanings; God made iron soft like wax, dough, or wet clay, shapeable by hand without heating or hammering.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r2.anchor: اللين ضد الخشونة يستعمل في الأجسام ثم يستعار للمعاني

BURSEVI:v7p209/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r3.claim: Alternatively, iron was soft relative to David’s exceptional bodily strength; he was powerfully strong though not bulky, as indicated by the description in Sūrat Ṣād.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r3.anchor: أو جعلناه بالنسبة إلى قوته التي آتيناها إياه لينا كالشمع بالنسبة إلى سائر قوى البشرية وكان داود أوتي شدة قوة في الجسد وإن لم يكن جسيما

BURSEVI:v7p209/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r6.claim: A report says David disguised himself to ask people’s opinion; an angel in human form faulted his use of the public treasury, prompting him to ask for a way to earn independently, whereupon God taught him armor-making.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r6.anchor: كان عليه السلام حين ملك على بني إسرائيل يخرج متنكرا فيسأل الناس ما تقولون في داود

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r4.claim: The softening of iron signifies the softening of David’s heart; the full coats are profound judgments flowing from his heart through his tongue.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r4.anchor: يشير إلى إلانة قلبه والسابغات الحكم البالغة التي ظهرت ينابيعها من قلبه على لسانه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r9.claim: God’s favor to David and Solomon sets a precedent for what He granted Muhammad; the discourse then turns to Saba’s fate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى نعمته على داود وسليمان احتجاجا على ما منح محمدا، أي لا تستبعدوا هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Ibn Zayd, and others explain awibī as “glorify with him”: David praises God and the mountains echo his praise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد وغيرهم معناه سبحي معه أي يسبح هو وترجع هي معه التسبيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r11.claim: Another explanation takes awibī as “travel with him”: taʾwīb is repeated daytime travel after night travel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p406#2/r11.anchor: وقيل معناه سيري معه لأن التأويب سير النهار كان الإنسان يسير بالليل ثم يرجع السير بالنهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r1.claim: The quoted line about traveling toward the enemy uses taʾwīb for daytime travel, supporting the travel interpretation; its attribution to the poet is given with the preceding segment’s citation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r1.anchor: يومان يوم مقامات وأندية ... ويوم سير إلى الأعداء تأويب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r2.speaker: ابن أبي مقبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Miqbal’s line uses awibū al-sayr for resuming the journey after the sun’s rays have passed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r2.anchor: ومنه قول ابن أبي مقبل: [الطويل] لحقنا بحي أوبوا السير بعد ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r3.speaker: مروح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r3.claim: Marwāḥ says awibī means “glorify” in Abyssinian, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak and unrecognized.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r3.anchor: وقال مروح أوبي سبحي بلغة الحبشة. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف غير معروف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says David’s lamenting call drew answers from mountains and birds that gathered above him; this is when mountain echoes began to be heard.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r4.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: المعنى نوحي معه والطير تسعدك على ذلك، قال فكان داود إذا نادى بالنياحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ūbī with ḍamma on hamza and a still wāw, meaning “return with him” in travel or praise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وابن أبي إسحاق «أوبي» بضم الهمزة وسكون الواو أي ارجعي معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r6.claim: The non-rational plural mountains take the feminine singular imperative, as such plurals regularly do; compare “O horses of God, ride” and Ṭā Hā 20:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r6.anchor: وأمر الجبال كما تؤمر الواحدة المؤنثة لأن جمع ما لا يعقل كذلك يؤمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r7.speaker: الأعرج وعاصم بخلاف وجماعة من أهل المدينة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r7.claim: Al-Aʿraj, ʿĀṣim in one transmission, and a group of Medinese readers read al-ṭayr in the nominative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وعاصم بخلاف وجماعة من أهل المدينة «والطير» بالرفع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r8.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r8.claim: For the accusative reading, al-Kisāʾī connects the birds to “favor.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r8.anchor: فقيل ذلك عطف على فضلا وهو مذهب الكسائي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r9.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r9.claim: Sībawayh connects the accusative to the syntactic position of the vocative, which is accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r9.anchor: وقال سيبويه هو على موضع قوله يا جبال لأن موضع المنادى المفرد نصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr treats the accusative as governed by an omitted verb: “We subjected the birds.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: نصبها بإضمار فعل تقديره وسخرنا الطير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r11.claim: Qatāda and others report that iron was like wax for David, so he needed no fire to work it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r11.anchor: وروى قتادة وغيره أن الحديد كان له كالشمع لا يحتاج في عمله إلى نار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r12.claim: Another explanation is that God gave David the strength to bend iron.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r12.anchor: وقيل أعطاه قوة يثني بها الحديد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r13.claim: A report says David met an angel disguised as a man while secretly asking about himself; the angel said he was a good king but should earn his living by labor, so God taught him armor-making. David made armor worth a thousand dirhams daily, expanded his household’s means, and spent a third on public needs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r13.anchor: وروي أنه لقي ملكا وداود يظنه إنسانا وداود متنكر خرج ليسأل الناس عن نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r1.claim: God’s favor to David included prophethood, the Psalms, and the subjection of mountains and birds, among other blessings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r1.anchor: وهو النبوة والزبور وتسخير الجبال والطير إلى غير ذلك مما أنعم الله به عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r2.speaker: الحلبي عن عبد الوارث
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r2.claim: Al-Ḥalabī, transmitting from ʿAbd al-Wārith, reads awbī with ḍamma on the hamza and a light, ungeminated wāw.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r2.anchor: وروى الحلبي عن عبد الوارث أوبي بضم الهمزة وتخفيف الواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the command to the mountains as returning and echoing glorification with David.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى وقلنا يا جبال أوبيء معه أي رجعي معه والمعنى سبحي معه ورجعي التسبيح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r4.claim: On the reading awbī, the mountains repeatedly return to glorification whenever David repeats it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r4.anchor: معناه عودي في التسبيح معه كلما عاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives taʾwīb from traveling all day and stopping at night; the command suggests persisting in glorification through the day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة أوبي أي سبحي واصل التأويب في السير وهو ان يسير النهار كله وينزل ليلا فكأنه أراد ادأبي النهار كله بالتسبيح إلى الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r6.speaker: أبو رزين، أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي، أبو العالية، ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r6.claim: Abū Razīn, al-Sulamī, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read al-ṭayr in the nominative; the passage also contrasts the accusative reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وابو العالية وابن أبي عبلة والطير بالرفع فأما قراءة النصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ construes the accusative as coordinated with God’s favor: God also subjected the birds to David.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r7.anchor: فأما قراءة النصب فقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء هو عطف على قوله ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا والطير أي وسخرنا له الطير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows the accusative as a vocative, with the birds coordinated to the syntactic position of the mountains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج ويجوز ان يكون نصبا على النداء كأنه قال دعونا الجبال والطير فالطير معطوف على موضع الجبال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r9.claim: For the nominative, al-Zajjāj allows coordination with the implied subject of awbī, so the birds join the mountains in glorifying.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r9.anchor: وأما الرفع فمن جهتين إحداهما ان يكون نسقا على ما في أوبي فالمعنى يا جبال رجعي التسبيح معه أنت والطير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj also analyzes the nominative as a direct address: mountains and birds are both called to glorify with David.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r10.anchor: والثانية على النداء المعنى يا جبال ويا أيها الطير أوبي معه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that birds glorified with David and that creatures listened to his recitation and wept with his weeping.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس كانت الطير تسبح معه إذا سبح وكان إذا قرأ لم تبق دابة إلا استمعت لقراءته وبكت لبكائه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r12.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r12.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says David called the mountains to glorify and the birds to respond, then recited the Psalms beautifully among them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p435/r12.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه كان يقول للجبال سبحي وللطير أجيبي ثم يأخذ هو في تلاوة الزبور بين ذلك بصوته الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r1.claim: God made iron pliable for David.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r1.anchor: أي جعلناه لينا قال قتادة سخر الله له الحديد بغير نار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r2.claim: Qatāda says iron was subjected to David without fire: he shaped it by hand without heating or hammering, and was the first to make mail armor; previously armor was plates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436/r2.anchor: قال قتادة سخر الله له الحديد بغير نار فكان يسويه بيده لا يدخله النار ولا يضربه بحديدة وكان اول من صنع الدروع وكانت قبل ذلك صفائح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r1.claim: God's favor on David combined prophethood, secure kingship, equipped armies, and a magnificent voice; mountains praised with him, while birds stopped and answered in varied languages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r1.anchor: مما آتاه من الفضل المبين، وجمع له بين النبوة والملك المتمكن، والجنود ذوي العدد والعدد، وما أعطاه ومنحه من الصوت العظيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r2.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet heard Abu Musa reciting at night, stopped to listen, and said Abu Musa had been given one of David's flutes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r2.anchor: وفي الصحيح أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع صوت أبي موسى الأشعري يقرأ من الليل، فوقف فاستمع لقراءته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r3.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi says he never heard a cymbal, oud, or string sound more beautiful than Abu Musa al-Ashari's voice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان النهدي: ما سمعت صوت صنج ولا بربط ولا وتر أحسن من صوت أبي موسى الأشعري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد وغير واحد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others gloss awībī as glorify.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r4.anchor: معنى قوله: {أوبي} أي: سبحي. قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وغير واحد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r5.claim: Abu Maysara claims that awībī means glorify in the Ethiopian language; Ibn Kathir questions this explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r5.anchor: ميسرة أنه بمعنى سبحي بلسان الحبشة. وفي هذا نظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says Arabic taʾwīb means returning or repeating, so the mountains and birds were told to echo their sounds with David.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r6.anchor: فإن التأويب في اللغة هو الترجيع، فأمرت الجبال والطير أن ترجع معه بأصواتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r7.speaker: أبو القاسم عبد الرحمن بن إسحاق الزجاجي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaji interprets the command as traveling with David through the whole day; taʾwīb is all-day travel and isʾād all-night travel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r7.anchor: {يا جبال أوبي معه} أي: سيري معه بالنهار كله، والتأويب: سير النهار كله، والإسآد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir calls al-Zajjaji's interpretation very unusual and remote in context, preferring that the mountains repeat praise with David.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497/r8.anchor: لكنه بعيد في معنى الآية هاهنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري، وقتادة، والأعمش وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r1.claim: Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, al-Aʿmash, and others say David could twist iron by hand like threads, without heating or hammering it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r1.anchor: قال الحسن البصري، وقتادة، والأعمش وغيرهم: كان لا يحتاج أن يدخله نارا ولا يضربه بمطرقة، بل كان يفتله بيده مثل الخيوط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r11.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r11.claim: Wahb's account says David's psalm recitation captivated wild animals and that Satanic instruments imitated its kinds of sound; David had seventy tones in his throat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r11.anchor: وقال: إن الله أعطى داود شيئا لم يعطه غيره من حسن الصوت، إنه كان إذا قرأ الزبور تسمع الوحش

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r1.speaker: يعقوب الحضرمي وعبيد بن عمير
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r1.claim: Yaqub al-Hadrami and Ubayd ibn Umayr read al-ṭayr in the nominative, coordinating it with the mountains as a vocative.
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب الحضرمي وعبيد بن عمير: (الطير) بالرفع

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r2.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r2.claim: The general reading has al-ṭayr accusative; one analysis supplies “We subjected the birds,” as in a poetic example with an omitted verb for watering.

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r3.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r3.claim: Alī ibn ʿĪsā analyzes the accusative as coordination with the syntactic position of the vocative, “I call the mountains and birds,” but says the first analysis is better because it follows the vocative’s surface form.
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r3.anchor: وتقديره: أنادي الجبال والطير، قال علي بن عيسى: والأول أجود؛ لأن الحمل على لفظ المنادى أشكل

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r4.claim: Other accusative analyses treat the bird as governed by an omitted preposition (“with the birds”) or coordinate it with the verb, with mountains and birds responding to David.
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r4.anchor: وقيل: نصب بنزع الخافضة أي: مع الطير. وقيل: هو عطف على الفعل، تقديره: آتيناه فضلا الجبال تؤوب معه والطير

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r5.claim: Abu Ali understands the text as “We said, ‘Mountains, echo with him,’” with the birds also intended by the same command.
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r5.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: قلنا: يا جبال أوبي معه، وعنينا الطير بمثل هذا القول، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v8p5785/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r6.claim: Abu Muslim says the birds are accusative because they too are commanded, coordinated with the mountains’ command rather than with the sense of being subdued alongside them.
JISHUMI:v8p5785/r6.anchor: وقيل: نصب؛ لأنه مأمور، وعطف على الجبال لا على معنى التذليل بالتأويب معه، تقديره: أمرنا الجبال والطير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r1.claim: “O mountains” can be apposed to “favor,” or to “We gave” with an implied “Our saying” or “We said.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r1.anchor: يا جبال } إما أن يكون بدلا من { فضلا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r2.claim: Two readings are given for “repeat with him,” both derived from taʾwīb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( أوبي ) و ( أوبي ) من التأويب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r3.claim: Aوب means return: the mountains repeat glorification with David or return to it whenever he does, since repetition is itself a return.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r3.anchor: والأوب : أي رجعي معه التسبيح . أو ارجعى معه في التسبيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r4.claim: God creates glorification in the mountains as He created speech in the tree; their sound is heard like a glorifier’s, a miracle for David.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r4.anchor: أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يخلق فيها تسبيحا كما خلق الكلام في الشجرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, David lamented his sin with mournful repetition, and mountains echoed him as birds joined their voices.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : كان ينوح على ذنبه بترجيع وتحزين ، وكانت الجبال تسعده على نوحه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r6.claim: “And the birds” is read in the nominative and accusative.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r7.speaker: author
