KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r7.claim: The birds may coordinate with the mountains’ wording or grammatical position, be a comitative object, or coordinate with “favor,” meaning they too were subjected to David.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r7.anchor: وعطفا على لفظ الجبال ومحلها . وجوزوا أن ينتصب مفعولا معه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r8.claim: The command is more majestic than a plain statement that God gave David favor and caused mountains and birds to repeat with him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r8.anchor: كم بينهما . ألا ترى إلى ما فيه من الفخامة التي لا تخفى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r9.claim: Addressing mountains as rational beings who obey and answer displays divine lordship and majesty, showing all creatures and inanimate things submit to God’s will.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r9.anchor: حيث جعلت الجبال منزلة منزلة العقلاء الذي إذا أمرهم أطاعوا وأذعنوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r10.claim: God made iron as soft as clay, dough, or wax for David to shape by hand without fire or hammering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r10.anchor: وجعلناه له لينا كالطين والعجين والشمع ، يصرفه بيده كيف يشاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r11.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r11.claim: Another explanation says iron was pliable in David’s hand because he had extraordinary strength.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r11.anchor: وقيل : لأن الحديد في يده لما أوتي من شدة القوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.claim: One of seven interpretations of the favor given to David is prophethood.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r2.claim: A second interpretation is the Psalms.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r3.claim: A third interpretation is the ability to judge fairly.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r4.claim: A fourth interpretation is discernment and intelligence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r5.claim: A fifth interpretation is mercy toward the weak.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.claim: A sixth interpretation is a beautiful voice.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.claim: A seventh interpretation is the subjection of the mountains and birds to David.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada gloss the command to the mountains as “glorify with him.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.anchor: أحدها : سبحي معه , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets it as traveling with David; the journey might last all day or all night, though another view limits it to daytime.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r10.claim: A third sense is to return when David returns, with a poetic line using taʾwīb for repeated returning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r10.anchor: الثالث : ارجعي إذا رجع , قال الشاعر : يومان يوم مقامات وأندية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r11.claim: Qatada says David could work iron as though it were clay, without heating it in fire or striking it with a hammer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r11.anchor: قال قتادة كان يعمل به كما يعمل بالطين لا يدخله النار ولا يضربه بمطرقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r12.claim: Al-Mawardi also suggests God made iron easy for David to shape however he wished while it retained its nature; the idiom “so-and-so has become pliant to you” means he has become easy to deal with.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r12.anchor: ويحتمل وجها آخر أنه سهل له الحديد أن يعمل منه ما شاء وإن كان على جوهره وطبعه من قولهم قد لان لك فلان إذا تسهل عليك

MUJAHID:v2p523#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p523#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p523#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the mountains' command as glorifying God along with David.
MUJAHID:v2p523#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ يا جبال أوبي معه ﴾ يقول سبحي معه

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r1.claim: David’s فضل means prophethood; God also gave him the Psalms and subjected mountains, birds, and iron to him.
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r1.anchor: النبوة والزبور وما سخر له من الجبل والطير والحديد

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r2.claim: The mountains are told to glorify with David, remembering the Lord with him through praise.
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r2.anchor: سبحي معه مع داود، عليه السلام، يقول: اذكري الرب مع داود، وهو التسبيح

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r3.claim: David plaited iron like dough without fire and made long coats of mail.
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r3.anchor: يضفر الحديد ضفر العجين من غير نار، فيتخذها دروعا طوالا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r1.claim: Ya jibalu may be an appositive to fadlan or attached to atayna on an implied we said or we called.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r1.anchor: بدل من فضلا أو من آتينا بتقدير قولنا يا جبال أو قلنا يا جبال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r2.claim: Awwibi derives from taʾwib, returning; God creates glorification in the mountains, heard like a person's, as a miracle for David.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r2.anchor: من التأويب رجعى معه التسبيح ومعنى تسبيح الجبال ان الله يخلق فيها تسبيحا فيسمع منها كما يسمع من المسبح معجزة لداود

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r3.claim: The birds may be coordinated with the grammatical position or expressed form of mountains.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r3.anchor: عطف على محل الجبال والطير عطف على لفظ الجبال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r4.claim: The wording presents mountains as intelligent beings who obey and answer, showing all creatures submit to God's will; a plain phrasing would lose this grandeur.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r4.anchor: جعلت الجبال بمنزلة العقلاء الذين إذا أمرهم بالطاعة أطاعوا وإا دعاهم أجابوا اشعار بأنه مامن حيوان إلا وهو منقاد لمشيئة الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r5.claim: God made iron pliant like kneaded clay, so David shaped it by hand without fire or hammer.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r5.anchor: وجعلناه له لينا كالطين المعجون يصرفه بيده كيف يشاء من غير نار ولا ضرب بمطرقة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r6.claim: Another view says iron softened because David was granted great strength.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p321#3/r6.anchor: وقيل لان الحديد فى يده لما أوتى من شدة القوة

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r1.claim: The passage answers deniers of Muhammad's prophethood: sending messengers is not unprecedented; God sent earlier messengers, supported them with miracles, and punished opponents.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r1.anchor: بين لمنكري نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن إرسال الرسل ليس أمرا بدعا

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r3.claim: Faḍlan means something by which God favored David above others.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r3.anchor: فضلا } أي أمرا فضلناه به على غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r4.claim: The first of nine reported explanations of David's special favor is prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r4.anchor: واختلف في هذا الفضل على تسعة أقوال: الأول: النبوة

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r5.claim: The second reported explanation of the special favor is the Psalter.

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r6.claim: A third explanation is knowledge, as in the verse saying God gave David and Solomon knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r6.anchor: الثالث: العلم، قال الله تعالى: ولقد آتينا داود وسليمان علما

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r7.claim: A fourth explanation is strength, supported by the description of David as possessing strength.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r7.anchor: الرابع: القوة، قال الله تعالى: واذكر عبدنا داود ذا الأيد

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r8.claim: A fifth explanation is that the mountains and people were subjected to David.

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r9.claim: A sixth explanation is David's repentance and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r9.anchor: السادس: التوبة، قال الله تعالى: فغفرنا له ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r10.claim: A seventh explanation is judgment with justice, supported by the address appointing David as vicegerent on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r10.anchor: السابع: الحكم بالعدل، قال الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r11.claim: An eighth explanation is the softening of iron for David.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r11.anchor: الثامن: إلانة الحديد، قال تعالى: { وألنا له الحديد

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r12.claim: A ninth explanation is David's beautiful voice; the passage also describes his face as beautiful.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r12.anchor: التاسع: حسن الصوت، وكان داود عليه السلام ذا صوت حسن

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r13.claim: The author treats beautiful voice as God's gift and connects it with ‘He increases creation as He wills.’
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r13.anchor: وحسن الصوت هبة من الله تعالى وتفضل منه

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r14.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r14.claim: The Prophet told Abu Musa that he had been given one of the flutes of David's family, praising his voice.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r14.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي موسى

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r15.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r15.claim: Scholars explain mizmar and mizmūr as a beautiful voice; the instrument is named mizmar for its sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r15.anchor: قال العلماء: المزمار والمزمور الصوت الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r16.claim: Many jurists approve beautifying and melodically varying Qur'an recitation; the author says he discussed this in the introduction.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r16.anchor: وقد استحسن كثير من فقهاء الأمصار القراءة بالتزيين والترجيع

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r17.claim: The command means God told the mountains to repeat glorification with David, as another verse says they glorified with him at evening and sunrise.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r17.anchor: أي وقلنا يا جبال أوبي معه، أي سبحي معه

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r18.speaker: أبو ميسرة
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r18.claim: Abu Maysara says the word is Ethiopian for glorification.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r18.anchor: قال أبو ميسرة: هو التسبيح بلسان الحبشة

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r19.claim: The mountains' glorification means God created it in them as He created speech in a tree, making their audible response a miracle for David.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r19.anchor: ومعنى تسبيح الجبال: هو أن الله تعالى خلق فيها تسبيحا

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r20.claim: Another interpretation is to travel with David during the day's full journey and stop when night comes.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10/r20.anchor: وقيل: المعنى سيري معه حيث شاء من التأويب

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r1.speaker: ابن مقبل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r1.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line uses awbū al-sayr for completing a day's journey, supporting the travel interpretation.

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r2.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others read awib with the sense ‘return with him,’ from the verb āba, to return.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: «أوبي معه» أي رجعي معه

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r3.claim: A further interpretation is that mountains move with David through the day as he moves; when he recites the Psalter, mountains sound with him and birds listen.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى تصرفي معه على ما يتصرف عليه داود بالنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r4.claim: Wahb says the mountains echoed David's lamenting call and birds gathered above; their support strengthened his voice whenever he faltered.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r4.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: المعنى نوحي معه والطير تساعده

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r5.claim: Wahb adds that David's voice was so beautiful that wild animals gathered and flowing water stopped to listen.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#2/r5.anchor: وكان قد أعطي من الصوت ما يتزاحم الوحوش من الجبال

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r1.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ونصر عن عاصم وابن هرمز ومسلمة بن عبد الملك
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r1.claim: These readers use the nominative, coordinating with the word mountains or the pronoun in awibi; separation by maʿa makes the latter possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r1.anchor: «والطير» بالرفع قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق ونصر عن عاصم

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r2.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r2.claim: The other readers use the accusative, which Sibawayh parses as coordination with the grammatical position of the vocative yā-jibāl.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r2.anchor: الباقون بالنصب عطفا على موضع «يا جبال» أي نادينا الجبال

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r3.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala parses the accusative by supplying an implicit verb meaning ‘We subjected the birds to him.’
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r3.anchor: وعند أبي عمرو بن العلاء بإضمار فعل على معنى وسخرنا له الطير

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r4.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi connects the word to ‘We gave David,’ meaning that God also gave him the birds.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو معطوف، أي وآتيناه الطير

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r5.claim: Al-Nahhas says the word can be an object of accompaniment, like saying the water and the log floated together.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r5.anchor: مفعولا معه، كما تقول: استوى الماء والخشبة

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows coordination like ‘I stood with Zayd’; the meaning is that the mountains and birds glorify with David.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r6.anchor: وسمعت الزجاج يجيز: قمت وزيدا، فالمعنى أوبي معه

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says iron became like wax in David's hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صار عنده كالشمع

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r8.claim: Hasan says the iron became like dough, so David could shape it without fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: كالعجين، فكان يعمله من غير نار

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r9.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says iron was like wet clay, dough, or wax and could be shaped without fire or hammering.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r9.anchor: وقال السدي: كان الحديد في يده كالطين المبلول والعجين والشمع

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r10.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r10.claim: Muqatil says David could finish a coat of armor in part of a day or night, valued at one thousand dirhams.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r10.anchor: مقاتل: وكان يفرغ من الدرع في بعض اليوم أو بعض الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r11.claim: An account says David went out in disguise to learn what Israelites thought of him and met a king whom he took for a man; the king said he lived from the treasury.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r11.anchor: وقيل: أعطي قوة يثني بها الحديد، وسبب ذلك أن داود

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r12.claim: In the account, the king says David's virtues would be complete if he earned his living by hand; David asks God to teach and ease a craft and is taught armor making.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r12.anchor: فقال له الملك «نعم العبد لولا خلة فيه» قال داود

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r13.claim: The account says David made armor worth a thousand dirhams per day, supported his household and the poor, spent a third on public needs, and was first to make armor, previously made as plates.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r13.anchor: فكان يصنع الدرع فيما بين يومه وليلته يساوي ألف درهم

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r14.claim: A further report says David sold each coat of armor for four thousand dirhams.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r14.anchor: ويقال: إنه كان يبيع كل درع منها بأربعة آلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r15.claim: Dirʿ is feminine for armor used in war, but masculine for a woman's breastplate.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r15.anchor: والدرع مؤنثة إذا كانت للحرب. ودرع المرأة مذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r16.claim: The verse supports people of excellence learning crafts: work adds humility, independence, and lawful earnings without indebtedness to others.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#3/r16.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على تعلم أهل الفضل الصنائع

QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#4/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#4/r1.claim: The Prophet said the best food a person eats is from his own labor, and that David, God's prophet, ate from his own labor.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:10#4/r1.anchor: إن خير ما أكل المرء من عمل يده وإن نبي الله داود كان يأكل من عمل يده

QASHANI:34:10-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r1.claim: David symbolizes the spirit, given rank, the glorification and intimacy of witnessing in love, increased worship and reflection, and scientific and practical perfections.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r1.anchor: بعلو الرتبة وتسبيح المشاهدة والمناغاة في المحبة مع مزيد العبادة والتفكر والكمالات العلمية العملية

QASHANI:34:10-11/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r2.claim: The mountains are bodily members, ordered to glorify through their particular obedience, practice, motions, stillness, and deeds.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r2.anchor: من الانقياد والتمرن في الطاعات بالحركات والسكنات والأفعال والانفعالات التي أمرناك بها

QASHANI:34:10-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r3.claim: The birds are spiritual powers, glorifying through holy remembrances, perceptions, reasoning, receptivity, and illumination from disembodied spirits.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r3.anchor: وطير القوى الروحانية بالتسبيحات القدسية من الأذكار والإدراكات

QASHANI:34:10-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r4.claim: The iron softened for David is elemental bodily nature.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r4.anchor: وألنا له } حديد الطبيعة الجسمانية العنصرية

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r1.claim: “From Us” highlights David’s special rank: although God’s favors are general, prophecy is a particular gift bestowed on some.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r1.anchor: فكذلك إيتاء الله الفضل عام لكن النبوة من عنده خاص بالبعض

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the call to the mountains as an apposition to “favor,” so the favor means God’s saying, “O mountains, echo with him.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري : { من جبال } بدل من قوله : { فضلا }

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows “O mountains” to be an apposition to “We gave,” meaning, “We said: O mountains.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r3.anchor: أو من آتينا ومعناه قلنا يا جبال

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r4.claim: The verb is read with a doubled wāw from taʾwīb, or with a quiescent wāw and ḍamma on the hamza from awb; the former means repeated echoing, the latter return, and another gloss is traveling with him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r4.anchor: قرىء أوبي بتشديد الواو من التأويب وبسكونها وضم الهمزة أوبي من الأوب وهو الرجوع والتأويب الترجيع ، وقيل بأن معناه سيرى معه

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r5.claim: The phrase “they glorify” is explained as coming from sabāḥah, a particular kind of movement.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r5.anchor: قالوا : هو من السباحة وهي الحركة المخصوصة

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r6.claim: Al-ṭayr is read in the accusative, coordinated with the grammatical position of the vocative, or in the nominative, coordinated with its surface form.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r6.anchor: قرىء { والطير } بالنصب حملا على محل المنادى والطير بالرفع حملا على لفظه

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r7.claim: Mountains and birds are singled out because rocks seem immovable and birds seem prone to flee, making their agreement striking; if they comply, other things should do so more readily.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r7.anchor: ذكر الجبال ، لأن الصخور للجمود والطير للنفور تستبعد منهما الموافقة ، فإذا وافقه هذه الأشياء فغيرها أولى

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r8.claim: Some people nevertheless did not respond to David; their hearts were hardened even more than stones.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r8.anchor: ثم إن من الناس من لم يوافقه وهم القاسية قلوبهم التي هي أشد قسوة من الحجارة

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r9.claim: “We softened iron” can coordinate with the implied “We said” in the mountain address or with “We gave him favor.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r9.anchor: والمعطوف عليه يحتمل أن يكون قلنا المقدر في قوله يا جبال

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r10.claim: God made iron as soft as wax in David’s hand; since fire can soften and melt it, this is no cause to doubt God’s power.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r10.anchor: ألان الله له الحديد حتى كان في يده كالشمع وهو في قدرة الله يسير ، فإنه يلين بالنار

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r11.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r11.claim: One report says David asked God to make him independent of public funds, so God softened iron and taught him to make armor.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r11.anchor: قيل / إنه طلب من الله أن يغنيه عن أكل مال بيت المال فألان له الحديد وعلمه صنعة اللبوس

RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r12.claim: God chose armor because it protects the God-given soul and helps preserve honored human life; thus an armorer is better than an archer or swordsman.
RAZI-FULL:v25p212#2/r12.anchor: لأنه وقاية للروح التي هي من أمره وسعى في حفظ الآدمي المكرم عند الله من القتل

STUDYQURAN:34:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r1.claim: Bounty from God may mean prophethood and revelation.
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r1.anchor: Bounty from Us may be a reference to prophethood and revelation (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:34:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r2.claim: Alternatively, bounty may mean the judgment and knowledge God gave David and Solomon.
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r2.anchor: or to the judgment and knowledge that God is said to have given both David and Solomon

STUDYQURAN:34:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r3.claim: Mountains and birds are compelled to glorify God with David; because he is God's vicegerent, all things are contained in him in principle.
STUDYQURAN:34:10/r3.anchor: because he has been appointed as a vicegerent upon the earth

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r6.claim: David is a foreign name; another explanation derives it from the phrase meaning that he healed his wound.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r6.anchor: اسم أعجمي ، وقيل سمي داود لأنه داوى جرحه

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r7.claim: In a reported prayer, David asked for the ranks God gave His friends and prophets; after God said they had endured trials, David asked to be tested, faltered, and then received those ranks.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r7.anchor: قال في إحدى مناجاته : يا رب ، إني أرى في التوارة ما أعطيت لأوليائك وأنبيائك من الرتب

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r8.claim: One view identifies David’s favor as the answering of mountains and birds, which consoled him in grief and weeping.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r8.anchor: وكان في ذلك تنفيس في وقت حزنه وبكائه

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r9.claim: Another view is that the favor was David’s return to God after his lapse, with humility and apology.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r9.anchor: وقيل ذلك الفضل رجوعه إلى الله - في حال ما وقع له - بالتنصل والاعتذار

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r10.claim: Another explanation is that David witnessed his utter need and knew that no one but God could set his affairs right.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r10.anchor: ويقال هو شهوده موضع ضرورته وأنه لا يصلح أمره غيره

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r11.claim: Other explanations are David’s beautiful voice reading the Psalms, the sweetness of his intimate prayer, his good character with followers, and his just judgments.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r11.anchor: ويقال طيب صوته عند قراءة الزبور حتى كان ليرغب في متابعته من يسمع إليه . ويقال حلاوة صوته في المناجاة

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r12.claim: God commanded the mountains and birds to echo David as he went into the mountains and wilderness lamenting himself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r12.anchor: أمر الجبال والطير بمجاوبته حتى خرج إلى الجبال والصحارى ينوح على نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r13.claim: In a report, God calls David’s lapse blessed because he now comes to God like a sinner, whereas before he came like the obedient.
QUSHAYRI:v3p48#2/r13.anchor: فقال : إني ابتليتهم فصبروا ، فقال : إني أصبر على بلائك

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r1.claim: God says the sighs of sinners are dearer to Him than the cries of worshippers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r1.anchor: يا داود ، إن أنين المذنبين أحب إلي من صراخ العابدين

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r2.claim: David once asked God not to forgive sinners out of religious zeal; after his own lapse he prayed that sinners be forgiven, hoping to be forgiven among them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r2.anchor: اللهم لا تغفر للخاطئين ، غيرة منه وصلابة في الدين

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r3.claim: After God accepted David’s repentance, people, jinn, and birds assembled; when he raised his familiar voice, birds dispersed because his state no longer matched his former one.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r3.anchor: لما تاب الله عليه ، واجتمع الإنس والجن والطير بمجلسه ، ورفع صوته ، وأداره في حنكه

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r4.claim: God explains that David’s lapse brought estrangement, whereas his earlier obedience had brought intimacy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r4.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه هذه وحشة الزلة ، وتلك كانت أنس الطاعة

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r5.claim: The spiritual meaning belonged to David himself, not to the mountains and birds that cried along with him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r5.anchor: ليس كل من صاح وراءه معنى ، فالمعنى كان مع داود لا مع الجبال والطير

QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r6.claim: God softened iron for David as a miracle and expanded his livelihood, so he could earn for himself rather than rely on his followers and burden them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p50/r6.anchor: ألان له الحديد ، وجعل ذلك معجزة له ، وجعل فيه توسعة رزقه ، ليجد في ذلك مكسبا ، ليقطع طمعه عن أمته

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r1.claim: God gave David a special bounty and commanded the mountains to glorify along with him whenever he glorified.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] قال: سبحي معه

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says taʾwīb in Arabic can mean returning, including returning at night to one's home and family.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r2.anchor: الرجوع، ومبيت الرجل في منزله وأهله

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r3.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r3.claim: A poet uses taʾwīb for a return journey, supporting the Arabic sense of returning.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r3.anchor: يومان يوم مقامات وأندية … ويوم سير إلى الأعداء تأويب

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r4.claim: Some read awibī from āba yaʾūbu, understanding it as move or turn along with David.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r4.anchor: وقد كان بعضهم يقرؤه: أوبي معه من آب يؤوب، بمعنى: تصرفي معه

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects that alternative reading because it conflicts with the reading transmitted by the authoritative readers.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r5.anchor: وتلك قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لخلافها قراءة الحجة

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command to the mountains as glorify with David.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] قال: سبحي معه

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r7.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says the mountains were commanded to glorify.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r7.anchor: أبي عبد الرحمن {يا جبال أوبي معه}

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r8.speaker: أبو ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r8.claim: Abū Maysara says the word means glorify in the Abyssinian language.

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r9.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as glorify with David.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {يا جبال أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] قال: سبحي معه

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r10.claim: Qatāda says the mountains glorify along with David when he glorifies.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {يا جبال أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] «أي سبحي معه إذا سبح»

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says the birds too glorified with David.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r11.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {يا جبال أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] قال: " سبحي معه؛ قال: والطير أيضا

TAB-FULL:v19p220/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r12.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also glosses the command as glorify.
TAB-FULL:v19p220/r12.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {يا جبال أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] قال: سبحي

TAB-FULL:v19p221/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk again glosses the command as glorify with David.
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: {يا جبال أوبي معه} [سبأ: 10] «سبحي معه»

TAB-FULL:v19p221/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r2.claim: The accusative al-ṭayr can coordinate with the mountains' implied nominative when the vocative particle is not repeated, treating the birds as directly called too, as Ibn Zayd says.
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r2.anchor: وفي نصب الطير وجهان: أحدهما على ما قاله ابن زيد من أن الطير نوديت كما نوديت الجبال

TAB-FULL:v19p221/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r3.claim: The accusative can instead reflect an omitted verb: the sense is that God said 'O mountains, glorify' and subjected the birds to David.
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r3.anchor: والآخر: فعل ضمير متروك استغني بدلالة الكلام عليه، فيكون معنى الكلام: فقلنا: يا جبال أوبي معه، وسخرنا له الطير

TAB-FULL:v19p221/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r4.claim: Raising al-ṭayr is also valid by coordination with the mountains implied in the verb 'glorify'.
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r4.anchor: وإن رفع ردا على ما في قوله «سبحي» من ذكر الجبال كان جائزا

TAB-FULL:v19p221/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r5.claim: It may also be raised in coordination with the mountains even though the birds were not addressed in the same way; a line addressing ʿAmr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk together illustrates the construction.
TAB-FULL:v19p221/r5.anchor: وقد يجوز رفع الطير وهو معطوف على الجبال، وإن لم يحسن نداؤها بالذي نوديت به الجبال

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r1.claim: The iron became like wet clay in David's hand, so he could shape it however he wished without heating or hammering it.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {وألنا له الحديد} [سبأ: 10] «سخر الله له الحديد بغير نار»

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r2.claim: Qatāda says God subjected iron to David without using fire.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {وألنا له الحديد} [سبأ: 10] «سخر الله له الحديد بغير نار»

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r3.claim: In another report, Qatāda says David shaped the iron by hand without fire or striking it with an iron tool.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وألنا له الحديد} [سبأ: 10] «كان يسويها بيده، ولا يدخلها نارا، ولا يضربها بحديدة»

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r1.claim: The passage presents alertness in returning to God after a stumble, through seeking pardon and making excuse.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r1.anchor: قال : فطنة ويقظة في الرجوع إلى ربه عند العثرة

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r2.claim: Grace is knowledge that the servant has no good apart from his Lord, whether turning toward Him or away, sinning or obeying.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : ﴿ فضلا ﴾ أي علما أن ليس للعبد

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r3.claim: God’s grace means trust in Him and reliance upon Him.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r3.anchor: قال جعفر في قوله : ﴿ ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا ﴾ قال : ثقة بالله

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r4.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r4.claim: One form of grace was the sweetness of David’s voice in intimate prayer.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r4.anchor: قال النهرجوري : حلاوة صوته في المناجاة

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r5.claim: Grace governs judgment, while justice governs decree.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : الحكم بالفضل والقضاء بالعدل

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r6.speaker: ابن خلال
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r6.claim: The greatest grace is for God to make servants know their true measure and enable them to return to Him.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r6.anchor: قال ابن خلال : افضل الفضل من الله إلى عباده أن يعرفهم اقدارهم

SULAMI:v2p154#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r7.speaker: عبد العزيز
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r7.claim: Grace includes love for the poor and mercy toward the weak.
SULAMI:v2p154#4/r7.anchor: قال عبد العزيز : حبا للمساكين ورحمة على الضعفاء

TAB-FULL:v1p13/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r3.speaker: أبو ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r3.claim: Abu Maysara explains أوبي معه as “glorify with him” in Abyssinian.
TAB-FULL:v1p13/r3.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ميسرة

TABATABAI:34:10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.claim: The passage recalls God's favors to David and Solomon and commands righteous work in gratitude: David received mountains, birds, and pliable iron; Solomon received the wind and obedient jinn.
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.anchor: إذ آتاهما الله من فضله إذ أنعم على داود بتسخير الجبال والطير معه

TABATABAI:34:10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r3.claim: These stories continue the resurrection argument: God manages people amid blessings, distinguishes gratitude from ingratitude, and will distinguish the groups in another life when this world does not.
TABATABAI:34:10/r3.anchor: وجه اتصال القصص على ما تقدم من حديث البعث أن الله هو المدبر لامور عباده وهم مغمورون في أنواع نعمه

TABATABAI:34:10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r4.claim: Faḍl means a gift, and taʾwīb means returning or repeating; here it is the mountains' repetition of praise with David, as 38:18–19 explains.
TABATABAI:34:10/r4.anchor: الفضل العطية والتأويب الترجيع من الأوب بمعنى الرجوع والمراد به ترجيع الصوت بالتسبيح

TABATABAI:34:10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r5.claim: Birds are coordinated with the syntactic position of “mountains” in the address.

TABATABAI:34:10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r6.claim: The address to mountains and birds stands in place of the gift of their subjugation: God subjected them to echo praise with David.
TABATABAI:34:10/r6.anchor: وقد وضع فيه الخطاب الذي خوطبت به الجبال والطير فسخرتا به موضع نفس التسخير الذي هو العطية وهو من قبيل وضع السبب موضع المسبب

TABATABAI:34:10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r7.claim: The author rejects the view of some that taʾwīb means travel and that the mountains moved wherever David went; the parallel passage says they praised with him.
TABATABAI:34:10/r7.anchor: ومنه يظهر فساد قول بعضهم أن الأوب بمعنى السير وأن الجبال كانت تسير معه حيثما سار

TABATABAI:34:10-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r1.claim: God made iron pliable for David despite its natural hardness.
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r1.anchor: أي وجعلناه لينا له على ما به من الصلابة

TABRISI:34:10-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14/r1.speaker: يعقوب وعبيد بن عمير والأعرج
TABRISI:34:10-14/r1.claim: Yaʿqūb, ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and al-Aʿraj read al-ṭayr nominative; the other readers read it accusative.
TABRISI:34:10-14/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وعبيد بن عمير والأعرج { والطير } بالرفع

TABRISI:34:10-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:34:10-14/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives two nominative analyses: birds coordinate with the yāʾ in “repeat,” or with the spoken form “mountains.”
TABRISI:34:10-14/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: أما الرفع في { والطير } ففيه وجهان

TABRISI:34:10-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن أبي عمرو
TABRISI:34:10-14/r3.claim: The accusative can coordinate with “favor,” meaning God granted David a favor and subjected birds to him; it can also be a vocative or mean “with the birds.”
TABRISI:34:10-14/r3.anchor: حكى ذلك أبو عبيدة عن أبي عمرو

TABRISI:34:10-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:10-14/r4.claim: Other accusative analyses coordinate birds with the implied vocative of mountains or take the phrase as “with the birds.”
TABRISI:34:10-14/r4.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون نصبا على النداء

TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r1.claim: Taʾwīb means repeated return in glorification; Salāma ibn Jandal’s verse uses it for going back and forth.
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r1.anchor: التأويب الترجيع بالتسبيح قال سلامة بن جندل

TABRISI:34:11-14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r10.claim: After mentioning servants who turn back to God, the passage turns to David and Solomon; God favored David with prophethood, scripture, decisive judgment, and miracles.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r10.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر عباد الله المنيبين إليه وصله سبحانه بذكر داود وسليمان

TABRISI:34:11-14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد
TABRISI:34:11-14/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Mujahid say God commanded the mountains to praise with David whenever he praised God, and they did so.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد قالوا: أمر الله الجبال أن تسبح معه

TABRISI:34:11-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r12.claim: The linguistic interpretation is “return the praise with him,” deriving awb from āba, yaʾūbu, to return.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r12.anchor: وتأويله عند أهل اللغة رجعي معه التسبيح من آب يؤوب

TABRISI:34:11-14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r13.claim: Alternatively, God caused praise to issue from the mountains as a miracle for David; birds may also praise if God grants them discernment to understand it.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون سبحانه فعل في الجبال ما يأتي به منها التسبيح معجزا له

TABRISI:34:11-12/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r1.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:34:11-12/r1.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says the mountains traveled with David wherever he went as a miracle; taʾwib means traveling by day.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك معجزا له عن الجبائي والتأويب السير بالنهار

TABRISI:34:11-12/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:34:11-12/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that the mountains complied with David’s purposes, such as digging wells, finding springs or ore, and laying roads.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r2.anchor: معناه ارجعي إلى مراد داود فيما يريده من حفر بئر واستنباط عين

TABRISI:34:11-12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:34:11-12/r3.claim: Qatada says iron became like wax in David’s hand, so he could shape it without fire or hammer.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r3.anchor: فصار في يده كالشمع يعمل به ما شاء من غير أن يدخله النار ولا أن يضربه بالمطرقة عن قتادة

FARRA:v2p355#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p355#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p355#2/r1.claim: The iron flowed for David, and he could fashion it as he wished, as easily as clay.
FARRA:v2p355#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: (وألنا له الحديد) أسيل له الحديد، فكان يعمل به ما شاء. كما يعمل بالطين.

THALABI:v8p71#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p71#2/r1.claim: The command to the mountains means: praise God with David whenever he praises Him.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r1.anchor: يا جبال أوبي معه: سبحي معه إذا سبح.

THALABI:v8p71#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r2.speaker: أبو ميسرة
THALABI:v8p71#2/r2.claim: Abu Maysara says the word is in the language of Abyssinia.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو ميسرة: هو بلسان الحبشة، وقال بعضهم:

THALABI:v8p71#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r3.speaker: قتادة وأبو عبيد
THALABI:v8p71#2/r3.claim: Qatada and Abu Ubayd understand the word as a form of returning: join David by returning to praise.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r3.anchor: فهذا معنى قول قتادة وأبي عبيد،

THALABI:v8p71#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v8p71#2/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih glosses the command as making an echoing sound with David.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r4.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: نوحي معه.

THALABI:v8p71#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p71#2/r5.claim: The mountains answered David's chanting with their echo, while birds gathered above him; people have heard the mountain echo ever since.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r5.anchor: وكان إذا نادى بالنياحة أجابته الجبال بصداها وعكفت الطير عليه من فوقه، فصدى الجبال الذي يسمعه الناس من ذلك اليوم.

THALABI:v8p71#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r6.speaker: ويقال
THALABI:v8p71#2/r6.claim: A report says the mountains joined David's praise; after he resolved to worship as no one had before, God comforted him through their praise, and an angel showed him that God hears even a worm's faint rustle.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r6.anchor: ويقال: إن داود كان إذا سبح الله جعلت الجبال تجاوبه بالتسبيح نحو ما يسبح.

THALABI:v8p71#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r7.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v8p71#2/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybi derives the term from travel all day and stopping at night; Ibn Muqbil's verse uses it for a day-long journey, applied here to praising throughout the day.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r7.anchor: وقال القتيبي: أصله من التأويب في السير، وهو أن يسير النهار كله وينزل ليلا. قال ابن مقبل:

THALABI:v8p71#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p71#2/r8.speaker: العامة
THALABI:v8p71#2/r8.claim: The common accusative reading allows coordination with an implied verb or a vocative with the call particle omitted; birds may also be understood as commanded to join the praise.
THALABI:v8p71#2/r8.anchor: والطير قراءة العامة بالنصب، وله وجهان: أحدهما بالفعل، مجازه: وسخرنا له الطير، مثل قولك:

THALABI:v8p72/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r1.speaker: يعقوب
THALABI:v8p72/r1.claim: Yaqub is reported to read الطير nominative, coordinated with the mountains: the birds too are addressed to praise with David; the cited verse permits either case.
THALABI:v8p72/r1.anchor: وروي عن يعقوب بالرفع ردا على الجبال أي أوبي معه أنت والطير، كقول الشاعر:

THALABI:v8p72/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r2.claim: God made iron as pliable in David's hand as wet clay, dough, or wax, so he could shape it without fire or a hammer.
THALABI:v8p72/r2.anchor: فذكر أن الحديد كان في يده كالطين المبلول والعجين والشمع، يصرفه بيده كيف يشاء من غير إدخال نار ولا ضرب بحديد،

THALABI:v8p72/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r3.claim: A report says David sought a livelihood independent of the treasury after an angel disguised as a man criticized his use of public funds; God softened iron, taught him armor-making, and David sold each suit for four thousand, supporting his family and giving to the poor.
THALABI:v8p72/r3.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك على ما روي في الأخبار أن داود (عليه السلام) لما ملك بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v8p72/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r4.speaker: ويقال
THALABI:v8p72/r4.claim: Another explanation says iron was softened in David's hand because he had been given great strength.
THALABI:v8p72/r4.anchor: ويقال أيضا: إنما ألان الحديد في يده لما أعطي من القوة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r1.claim: Awwibī means praise God; taʾwīb originally described traveling all day and stopping at night.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r1.anchor: يا جبال أوبي معه} أي سبحي (1) . وأصله: التأويب في السير؛ وهو: أن تسير النهار كله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r2.speaker: ابن مقبل
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r2.claim: Ibn Muqbil's poem uses awb al-sayr for a journey continuing through the day, illustrating the root's travel sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#6/r2.anchor:
قال ابن مقبل:
[لحقنا بحي] أوبوا السير بعد ما ... دفعنا شعاع الشمس والطرف يجنح (2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r1.claim: God gave David a favor from Himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God bestowed on David what He had given to no one before or after him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد تفضلت عليه وأعطيته ما لم أعط أحدا قبله ولا بعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r3.claim: Muqātil identifies the favor as prophethood and scripture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني بالفضل: النبوة والكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the favor as prophethood and the worldly gifts David received.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني: النبوة وما أعطي من الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj treat the wording as elliptical: God said, “Mountains, echo back praise with him.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والزجاج: هو مختصر، المعنى: وقلنا يا جبال {أوبي معه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r6.claim: The exegetes unanimously explain awibi maʿahu as glorify along with David.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq derives awibi from āba yaʾūbu, to return: the mountains return the glorification with David.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أوبي معه معناه: رجعى، يقال: آب يؤوب إذا رجع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r8.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r8.claim: An unnamed alternative takes taʾwīb in Arabic as traveling all day until night, so the mountains praise with David throughout the day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: التأويب في كلام العرب. سير النهار كله إلى الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r9.speaker: سلامة بن جندل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r9.claim: Salāma b. Jandal’s verse uses taʾwīb for a day of travel toward the enemy, witnessing this travel sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r9.anchor: قال سلامة بن جندل: يومان يوم مقامات وأندية ... ويوم سير إلى الأعداء تأويب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr defines taʾwīb as traveling during the day and camping at night, in a report transmitted by Abū ʿUbayda.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r10.anchor: روى أبو عبيد عن أبي عمرو: التأويب أن يسير النهار وينزل الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r11.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers the all-day-travel interpretation: the mountains praise with David until night; al-Rāʿī’s verse supports the sense of continuing a journey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r11.anchor: وهذا اختيار ابن قتيبة، (وأنشد للراعي فقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r12.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r12.claim: The exegetes report that when David glorified, the mountains glorified along with him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r12.anchor: قال المفسرون: وكانت إذا سبح داود سبحت الجبال معه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r13.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r13.claim: Wahb reports that when David called, the mountains answered with their echoes, which is the echo people hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r13.anchor: وقال وهب (¬3): كان داود إذا نادى أجابته الجبال بصداها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r14.claim: One of Abū Isḥāq’s parses coordinates al-ṭayr with faḍlan: God gave David favor and subjected the birds for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r14.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون عطفا على قوله فضلا (¬5)، كأنه آتينا داود فضلا والطير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r15.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r15.claim: Yūnus transmits this coordination parse from Abū ʿAmr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r15.anchor: وروى هذا يونس عن أبي عمرو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r16.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r16.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the coordination as in the idiom, “I fed him food and gave him water.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p321#2/r16.anchor: وقال الفراء في هذا الوجه هو كقولك: أطعمته طعاما وسقيته ماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the accusative is like the vocative construction yā Zayd wa-al-Ṣalt aqbilā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: زعم النحويون أن سبيل نصبها كقولك: يا زيد والصلت أقبلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the second vocative is accusative because it lacks the vocative particle and is treated as diverted from its normal vocative form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r3.claim: A third parse makes al-ṭayr accusative by the implied maʿa, meaning the mountains and birds echo praise with David; the author calls Abū Isḥāq’s three parses the most apt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r3.anchor: الوجه الثالث: أن يكون الطير منصوبا على موضع مع، كما تقول: قمت وزيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the birds glorified with David when he glorified.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت الطير تسبح معه إذا سبح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the iron became like wax in David’s hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حتى صار عنده مثل السمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says David could take iron in his hand and it became like dough.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: كان يأخذ الحديد بيده، فيصير كأنه عجين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r7.claim: Qatāda says God softened iron for David, who worked it without fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: ألان (¬10) الله له الحديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r8.speaker: الأعمش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the iron was softened until it was like threads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r8.anchor: وقال الأعمش: ألين له حتى كان مثل الخيوط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r9.claim: Muqātil says David made linked coats of mail without tools or fire, completing one in part of a day or night worth one thousand dirhams.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p324/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان داود يسرد الدرع لا يفرغها بحديد ولا يدخلها النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r4.claim: God told the mountains to glorify with David; when he glorified, they answered, and birds gathered above him to join in the praise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r4.anchor: أي: قلنا يا جبال { أوبي معه } سبحي معه { والطير } كان إذا سبح جاوبته الجبال بالتسبيح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r5.claim: God made iron soft in David's hand like wet clay or dough.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:9-10/r5.anchor: جعلناه لينا في يده، كالطين المبلول والعجين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r2.claim: The favor given to David is prophethood.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r2.anchor: ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا} [سبأ: 10] النبوة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r3.claim: God’s address to the mountains means that He called out to them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the command to the mountains as telling them to glorify God with David.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r4.anchor: المعلى، عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد، قال: سبحي معه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r5.claim: The birds phrase recalls that God subjected the mountains and birds to glorify with David in 21:79.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r5.anchor: وسخرنا مع داود الجبال يسبحن والطير

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r6.claim: God softened iron for David, who could shape it by hand with three fingers like clay, without fire or a hammer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r6.anchor: ألانه الله له فكان يعمله بلا نار ولا مطرقة

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r1.claim: God granted David a special, extraordinary divine favor and miracle, beyond ordinary gifts and surpassing what earlier prophets had received; David was especially devoted in turning to God.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r1.anchor: yani alelâde değil, azamet-i ilâhiyeyi ayrıca bir husûsiyetle ifade eden

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r2.claim: David’s beautiful voice and glorious delivery made mountains and birds join his morning and evening glorification; this miraculous favor is explained through the parallel accounts in 21:79 and 38:18–19.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r2.anchor: onun sesine bütün dağlar ve kuşlar iştirak eder, çınlar öterlerdi.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r3.claim: Beautiful melody is not categorically blameworthy in Islam: licentious melodies are censured, whereas reciting the Quran with measured pacing and an improved voice is commanded.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r3.anchor: Bu güzel sanatı İslâm’da sûret-i mutlakada mezmum zannedenler olmuştur. Fakat bilmek lâzım gelir ki mezmum olan lühûn-ı fısktır.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r4.claim: Music directly affects the body and nerves through vibrating air; it gains spiritual value only when it helps the meaning of words reach the soul.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r4.anchor: Tegannî ancak bir kelimenin, bir kelâmın mânasını rûha duyurmaya hizmet etmesi itibariyledir ki rûhânî bir kıymet alabilir.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r5.claim: Licentious singers seek bodily excitement through sensual themes and meaningless sounds that extinguish spiritual awareness, while religion seeks a beautiful, meaningful, sacred, conscious life.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r5.anchor: Ehl-i fısk, hep şehevânî mevzularla cismânî heyecan aradığı için mânayı öldürerek sade a‘sâba basan kuru nağmelerle cismânî tesir arar.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r6.claim: Quran recitation should beautify the voice while preserving pronunciation, eloquence, and the meaning’s rhetorical subtleties; the prophetic expression lühûn-ı Arab is defined in recitation science through tajwid.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r6.anchor: elfâzın tecvîdini, fesâhatini bozmayarak, mânasını belâgatinin incelikleriyle duyurarak

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r7.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r7.claim: The Prophet praised a beautiful Quran reciter by saying that he had been given one of David’s psaltery-like melodies.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r7.anchor: Nitekim Kur’ân’ı güzel okuyan hakkında “Âl-i Dâvûd’un mezâmîrinden bir mizmar verilmiştir” diye sitâyiş buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r8.claim: The vocative Ya mountains treats them like rational beings, and the birds are coordinated in their place to express the meaning eloquently.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r8.anchor: zevi’l-ukūl gibi gösterilerek يَٰجِبَالُ diye nidâ, وَٱلطَّيْرَ onun mahalline atfedilmiştir.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r9.claim: Exegetes explain that iron softened in David’s hand like wax, so he could shape it at will without first heating or hammering it.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r9.anchor: Kızdırmaya, dövmeye muhtaç olmaksızın elinde balmumu gibi dilediği surete koyuverdi.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r10.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r10.claim: Razi says this should not be deemed impossible by God’s power: iron already softens and melts in fire, so no rational person should find it beyond divine power.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r10.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Allah’ın kudretinden bunu istib‘âd etmemelidir. Çünkü görülüyor, ateşte öyle yumuşuyor ve öyle münhal oluyor ki yazı yazılan mürekkeb hâline geliyor.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r11.claim: Some interpret the softening as discovery of extracting and melting iron with fire and tools; Elmalılı rejects this reading as arising from weak faith and distrust of divine power.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r11.anchor: Lâkin bu doğru değildir. İtikādının zaafı ve Allah’ın kudretine ‘adem-i i‘timâdı onu bu fikre sevketmiştir.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r12.claim: Still, the verse may allow that iron smelting was already known but David developed it into the fine craft of shaping iron thinly enough to make armor.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r12.anchor: Demirin keşfi ve izâbesi daha eski olsa gerektir. Fakat onu mum gibi dilediği şekle koyarak

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.claim: The parallel in 21:80 says armor-making protects people from battle; its address to you is directed to Muhammad’s community, suggesting the craft was passed on.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.anchor: buyurulmuştu ki bundan bu sanatın ahlâfa da yâdigâr kaldığı anlaşılıyor.

MAJAZ:v2p143/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p143/r1.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
MAJAZ:v2p143/r1.claim: One proposed accusative construction, attributed by Yunus to Abu Amr, coordinates al-ṭayr with an understood ‘We subjected the birds to him.’
MAJAZ:v2p143/r1.anchor: نصب من مكانين أحدهما فيما زعم يونس عن أبى عمرو على قوله:

MAJAZ:v2p143/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p143/r2.speaker: النحويون
MAJAZ:v2p143/r2.claim: Grammarians take al-ṭayr as accusative after an implied verb such as ‘I mean’; a definite noun cannot properly be called in a vocative here.
MAJAZ:v2p143/r2.anchor: والآخر على قول النحويين: يا زيد أقبل والصلت، نصب لأنه لا يحسن النداء

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r1.claim: David was a prophet sent to the Israelites and is described extensively in the Qur'an and Bible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r1.anchor: Hz. Dâvûd İsrâiloğulları’na gönderilmiş olan, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de ve Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te hakkında geniş bilgi verilen peygamberlerdendir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r2.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r2.claim: Some exegetes link the mention of David and Solomon here to the previous verse's münîb, ‘servant who turns to God.’
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r2.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bu ve müteakip âyetlerde Dâvûd ve Süleyman’dan söz edilmesi ile önceki âyetin sonunda geçen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r3.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r3.claim: The Qur'an also uses the related-root verb enābe for these two servants, in 38:24 and 38:34; both prophets exemplify turning to God with repentance and sincerity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r3.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah başka âyetlerde de (bk. Sâd 38/24, 34) bu iki kulu hakkında bu kelimeyle aynı kökten gelen enâbe fiilini kullanmıştır (Şevkânî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r4.claim: Reported glosses for David's special favor include prophethood, kingship, Zabur, knowledge, just judgment, courage, strength, bounty, fine voice, long life, reconciliation, influence over mountains, and armor-making that enabled self-support.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r4.anchor: Bu âyette fadl kelimesiyle ifade edilen ve Dâvûd’a verildiği bildirilen “müstesna lutuf”un ne olduğuna ilişkin belli başlı yorumlar şunlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r5.claim: The opening can also be translated simply as ‘We bestowed a favor on David,’ without calling it exceptional or superior.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r5.anchor: Bu kelimeye “müstesna, üstün” nitelemesi eklemeden âyetin ilk cümlesini “Andolsun biz Dâvûd’a bir lutufta bulunduk” şeklinde çevirmek de mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r6.claim: The imperative evvebe has dictionary senses such as returning, making something return, and walking.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r6.anchor: Âyette emir kipiyle geçen evvebe fiili sözlükte “dönme, döndürme, yürüme” gibi mânalara gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r7.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r7.claim: Exegetes generally understand the command as glorifying God, connecting that sense with the word's dictionary meanings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r7.anchor: Müfessirler genellikle –sözlük anlamlarıyla da bağ kurarak– burada “tesbih etme”nin kastedildiğini belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r8.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya considers weak the proposal that the word means glorification in the Habesh language.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r8.anchor: Habeş dilinde bunun “tesbih etme” anlamına geldiği görüşünü İbn Atıyye zayıf bulur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r9.claim: Tasbih expresses God's exaltedness and freedom from every imperfection, and may be conveyed in words or through one's state.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r9.anchor: Tesbîh Allah Teâlâ’nın yüceliğini, O’nun her türlü noksanlıktan münezzeh olduğunu ifade etmek demektir; bu da sözle veya hal ile olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r10.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r10.claim: One interpretation is that mountains and birds were commanded to accompany David with their own distinctive glorification.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r10.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bu varlıklara kendilerine özgü tesbih ile Dâvûd’a eşlik etmelerinin emredildiği kanaatindedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r11.speaker: Diğer bir yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that David's loud, melodious prayer while humbly supplicating made the mountains resound and birds join his chant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r11.anchor: Diğer bir yoruma göre ise âyette, Hz. Dâvûd’un kendini kullukta kusurlu bularak Allah’a yakarırken gür sesiyle dağı taşı inletmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r12.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r12.claim: Elmalılı says this verse and other evidence show that music is not categorically forbidden in Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r12.anchor: Elmalılı, bu âyet –ve başka bazı deliller– dikkate alındığında, mûsikinin İslâm’da mutlak biçimde yasaklandığı düşüncesinin yanlış olduğunun anlaşılacağına dikkat çeker

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r13.claim: Whether explained by ordinary experience or miracle, David's heartfelt, powerful supplication won God's favor, affected mountains and birds by God's will, and made him an example of sincere devotion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r13.anchor: Hz. Dâvûd’un yakarışı öylesine içten ve güçlü idi ki, bu yüce Allah’ın hoşnutluğunu kazanmasına, O’nun dilemesiyle dağlar ve kuşlar üzerinde bile etki meydana getirmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r14.claim: The lesson made explicit at the end of verse 11 is to keep God's oversight in mind and continually strive to do good and useful works.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r14.anchor: 11. âyetin sonunda açıkça ifade edildiği üzere, bütün bu anlatımlardan çıkarılması istenen sonuç, “kişinin ilâhî kontrol altında bulunduğu bilincini koruyarak daima iyi ve yararlı işler yapma çabası içinde olması gereği”dir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r15.speaker: Taberî; İbn Atıyye; Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r15.claim: Many commentaries say iron became like wax or clay in David's hand without heating, so he could shape it without tools such as a hammer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r15.anchor: Taberî, XXII, 66-67; İbn Atıyye, IV, 407; Râzî, XXV, 245-246

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r16.claim: God, who established natural laws, can grant extraordinary events to whomever he wills; transmitted proof would warrant accepting the reported details as given.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r16.anchor: Kuşkusuz tabiat kanunlarının da vâzıı olan yüce Allah dilediğinde istediği kulları için olağan üstülükler sağlayabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r17.claim: In light of the next verse, the phrase more plausibly means God directed David to work iron and gave him sufficient strength and special skill.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:10/r17.anchor: Fakat müteakip âyet dikkatle incelendiğinde, bu ifadenin Dâvûd’u demiri işlemeye yöneltme, bu konuda ona yeterli bir güç ve özel bir maharet verme anlamıyla açıklanması daha uygun görünmektedir

NAHHAS:v3p333/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p333/r5.claim: أوبي means echo the lament; the mountains answered David when he recited the Psalms, and the verb derives from آب يؤوب, to return.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r5.anchor: أي رجعي الحنين فكانت الجبال تجيبه إذا تلا الزبور وهو من آب يؤوب إذا رجع

NAHHAS:v3p333/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r6.speaker: الأعرج
NAHHAS:v3p333/r6.claim: Al-A'raj and Abu Abd al-Rahman read والطير nominative, coordinated either with جبال or with the pronoun in أوبي, supported by معه.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r6.anchor: ( والطير ) بالرفع قراءة الأعرج وأبي عبد الرحمن والرفع من جهتين

NAHHAS:v3p333/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
NAHHAS:v3p333/r7.claim: Abu Amr reads the word accusative with an understood verb: We subjected the birds to him.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r7.anchor: والنصب عند أبي عمرو بن العلاء بمعنى وسخرنا له الطير

NAHHAS:v3p333/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r8.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p333/r8.claim: Al-Kisa'i coordinates the accusative الطير with فضلا, meaning God gave him the birds.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي هو معطوف على فضلا أي آتيناه الطير

NAHHAS:v3p333/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r9.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p333/r9.claim: Sibawayh coordinates الطير with the syntactic position of the preceding phrase, as if God called the mountains and birds.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r9.anchor: وعند سيبويه معطوف على الموضع أي نادينا الجبال والطير

NAHHAS:v3p333/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p333/r10.claim: A comitative analysis is possible, like the water leveling with wood; Abu Ishaq allows a similar coordination with Zayd.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا معه كما تقول استوى الماء والخشبة

NAHHAS:v3p333/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p333/r11.claim: One report says David was first to have iron made pliable; another says he was given strength to bend it, and God knows best.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r11.anchor: قيل إنه أول من سخر له الحديد وقيل أعطي من القوة أنه كان يثني الحديد والله جل وعز أعلم بذلك

NAHHAS:v3p333/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r12.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v3p333/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says David handled iron like dough and made armor from it.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن وكان داود صلى الله عليه وسلم يأخذ الحديد فيكون في يده مثل العجين

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالنداءكلاسممضاففيهفهونصبع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالنداءكلاسممضاففيهفهونصبع.speaker: الأعرج
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنالنداءكلاسممضاففيهفهونصبع.claim: Al-Aʿraj recited wa-l-ṭayru in the nominative, illustrating coordination within the vocative construction.

BURHAN:v2p246/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p246/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p246/r4.claim: Mountains are commanded with the feminine singular form used for addressing inanimate things.
BURHAN:v2p246/r4.anchor: لأن جميع مالا يعقل كذلك يؤمر

ITQAN:v2p397/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p397/r13.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
ITQAN:v2p397/r13.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil glosses awwab as one who praises God in Ethiopian, and glosses “praise with him” as “glorify” in that language.
ITQAN:v2p397/r13.anchor: عن عمرو بن شرحبيل قال الأواب المسبح بلسان الحبشة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p75/r1.claim: God’s command to the mountains and birds to awbī with David means to praise with him, in keeping with the statement that all things glorify God though people do not understand their praise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.claim: David and Solomon received a kingdom, knowledge, wisdom, and many blessings without becoming arrogant; they remained grateful and obedient, so God continued increasing His favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.anchor: They never became arrogant and rebellious after receiving these favours; in fact, they continued to remain thankful and obedient to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.claim: The examples confront affluent, arrogant Quraysh with a choice: follow David and Solomon to merit favor, or follow Sheba and incur God's wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.anchor: Both these examples are presented before the affluent and arrogant among the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.claim: Since divine reward and punishment already operate in this world, the examples challenge people to explain why they consider them improbable in the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.anchor: if God’s law of reward and punishment comes into play in this world, why do they consider it to be improbable in the next world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r1.claim: Islahi says fuller accounts of God’s blessings on David and Solomon appeared in Sūrah Anbiyā’ and Sūrah Naml, so he gives only selected points here.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r1.anchor: Details of the blessings of God on the prophets David (sws) and Solomon (sws) have been mentioned earlier in Sūrah Anbiyā’ and Sūrah Naml.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r2.claim: Tawwīb means adding one’s tune to another’s, repeating another voice, or joining another in chanting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r2.anchor: The real meaning of بیوأََت is عیترج which is to add one’s tune into another’s, repeat another person’s voice

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r3.claim: The whole universe glorifies God and joins other glorifiers; David’s moving, melodious hymns drew creation into his chanting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r3.anchor: everything of this universe glorifies the Almighty and when it does so it also joins others who glorify God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r4.claim: The account of mountains and birds glorifying with David parallels Sūrah Anbiyā’ 21:79.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r4.anchor: In Sūrah Anbiyā’, the words used are:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r5.claim: The softened iron signifies David’s protective mail armor; the mail was light and wearable while still protecting its wearer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r5.anchor: The words اَّنَلَأَُو ُهَل َدیِدَحْال portray the weaponry of David viz. the Almighty softened iron for him.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r4.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r4.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads al-ṭayr in the accusative in the command to the mountains, construing it as a vocative.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p8/r4.anchor: وعيسى بن عمر -المتوفى سنة 149- يقرأ: {يا جبال أوبي معه والطير} 5 بنصب الطير
